^[Research Invitation] Speech Intervention Study for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate 【研究邀請】招募參與「唇顎裂兒童及青少年語音介入」之學術研究 - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
各位香港中文大學成員：
我們誠邀閣下及其子女參與由香港中文大學耳鼻喉科、頭頸外科進行的學術研究 。
研究題目： 「探索針對唇顎裂兒童及青少年的語音介入框架：隨機對照試驗」
研究目的：患有唇顎裂的兒童有較高風險出現語音/發音困難，這可能嚴重影響其說話清晰度。本研究旨在比較兩種不同的實證語音介入框架（線性與非線性語音介入）在改善這些語音錯誤方面的成效。
招募對象：
說廣東話的兒童及青少年 (4歲 – 17歲)；
4 至 17 歲，母語為廣東話嘅兒童及青少年。
患有唇顎裂，並有發音/語音問題。
於 24 個月大前已完成唇顎裂之修復手術；
無已知認知障礙，或任何會影響其獨立參與語音任務能力的醫療狀況。
研究程序：
全面評估：參與者將經歷全面的語音評估程序，包括多項標準化語音測試及填寫問卷。
個別治療：參與者將接受由專業言語治療師設計的語音治療方案。請注意，候補名單對照組的參與者將在主要研究觀察階段結束後接受治療。
錄影記錄：參與者的語音將被錄影，以作進一步記錄和分析。所有語音數據及錄音將受密碼保護並嚴格保密 。
費用與報酬：
潛在益處：參與者能透過治療方案提升整體說話清晰度，並為唇顎裂語音的臨床護理程序及機制提供貢獻。
參與費用：參與本研究無需支付任何額外費用。
聯絡方式： 如有興趣參與或有任何疑問，請致電 3943 9609 聯絡首席研究員 何皓賢先生。
感謝閣下對本研究計劃的興趣與支持。亦可以使用以下連結報名:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736537
此研究項目已獲香港中文大學 – 新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會（Joint CUHK-NTEC-CREC）批准。
Dear Members of the CUHK Community,
We are cordially inviting children and adolescents with Cleft Palate ± Lip to participate in a research study conducted by the Division of Speech Therapy (Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Study Title: Exploring Speech Intervention Frameworks for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate +/- Lip: A Randomized-Controlled Trial.
Children born with Cleft Palate ±Lip (CP±L) are at high risk for speech difficulties, such as glottal stops or backing errors, which can significantly impact how well they produce speech sounds and are understood. This study investigates the effectiveness of two different evidence-based speech intervention frameworks (Linear vs. Non-linear phonological intervention) in improving these speech outcomes.
Who Can Participate?
Cantonese-speaking children and adolescents (aged 4 to 17) with CP±L
Individuals exhibiting cleft speech errors that require intervention;
Primary repair of the palate done prior to 24 months old;
No known cognitive or hearing impairment, or other medical conditions that prevent independent participation in speech tasks.
What is Involved?
Comprehensive Assessment: Participants will undergo standardized speech assessments and questionnaires.
Treatment: Participants will receive speech therapy protocols designed by professional speech therapists. Please note that participants in the waitlist group will receive treatment after the primary study observation phase.
Recording: Speech sessions will be video-recorded for data analysis and will remain strictly confidential.
Benefits and Costs:
Potential Benefits: Improvement in overall speech clarity and contribution to the clinical management of cleft palate speech.
Costs: There is no additional cost to participate.
Contact Information: If you are interested or have questions, please contact Mr. Choco Ho (何皓賢), Speech Therapist and Principal Investigator, at 3943 9609 or click the link below:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736537
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC-CREC.

Recruiting CUHK Students as Climate Mentors — Join Project CLIMATE  - Department of Curriculum and Instruction
From: Eric Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cuhksdg@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear CUHK Students, Are you interested in climate action, sustainability, global learning, community engagement, education, communication, or working with young people?
Project CLIMATE: Community-engaged Learning, Inclusive Mentoring and AI-supported Transformative Education is recruiting CUHK students from all disciplines to become Climate Mentors. You will work alongside secondary-school students, teachers, community partners, and international youth peers in a local–global–local climate-learning journey.
As a Climate Mentor, you will have opportunities to:
Join mentor preparation and language-support workshops.
Facilitate small-group dialogue on Hong Kong climate and sustainability issues.
Support secondary students to prepare for English-language global dialogues with youth in partner schools.
Develop mentoring, communication, intercultural, teamwork, and community-engagement skills.
Learn about ethical and carefully governed uses of AI for dialogue preparation, rehearsal, and storytelling.
Contribute to student-led public communication and the Project CLIMATE showcase.
Connect climate issues with everyday life, community perspectives, the Sustainable Development Goals, and global dialogue.
Who can apply?
Current CUHK undergraduate or postgraduate students from any discipline.
Students with an interest in climate action, sustainability, education, youth work, communication, community engagement, design, science, social science, humanities, or global learning.
No prior specialist climate knowledge is required. Commitment, curiosity, respect for others, and willingness to learn are essential.
Indicative activities (exact dates to be finalized in accordance with the CUHK students' schedule)
2 half-day Climate Mentor preparation and 1 language-support workshops: December 2026 –January 2027
2 Local dialogue and mentoring activities with secondary students: February 2027
1 Global dialogue preparation and online exchange with international youth peers: March–April 2027
1 Public communication & exhibition preparation, and 1 student-led showcase: April–July 2027
Project CLIMATE will use generative AI only in an optional and carefully supervised support role. Students’ final reflections, captions, and core dialogue contributions will remain their own work and voice.
To express interest, please complete the registration form by November 13, 2026:
https://forms.gle/mN1By3Ng1eJsAHGz7
For enquiries, please contact: Dr Sally Wai-Yan Wan, Project Lead of Project CLIMATE: Community‐engaged Learning, Inclusive Mentoring and AI‐supported Transformative Education, Faculty of Education, CUHK Email:
cuhksdg@cuhk.edu.hk
We welcome students from diverse disciplines, backgrounds, and levels of prior experience. Join us to learn, listen, mentor, and communicate for a more sustainable future.

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: NGAI CHUN HO

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究: 隨機對照試驗
Effects of mindfulness-based training on the microbiome of older adults with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial
現正誠邀合資格人士報名參加！
We are now recruiting eligible participants to join our programme.
完成所有研究程序後，
參加者最多可獲價值$300的禮券
。
賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院現誠邀
60歲或以上
人士參加一項靜觀課程研究，探討靜觀訓練對有慢性壓力的長者腸道微生物群的影響。
很多長者長期承受慢性壓力，若未能妥善處理，對心理及生理健康均可能造成深遠影響。研究顯示，慢性壓力會擾亂腸道微生物群的平衡。雖然靜觀已被證實能有效改善心理健康，但目前仍甚少研究探討靜觀課程如何影響參與者的腸道微生物。
本項研究將在社區招募
138名年滿60歲的人士
，邀請他們參與專為長者而設的靜觀課程或健康教育課程，比較兩者在改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物方面的成效。
參加者將被隨機分派至以下其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組
參加者將接受為期八週、每週一次、每次約1小時30分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂課程將會錄音，以確保課程質素及一致性。
b) 健康教育組
參加者將接受為期八週、每週一次、每次約1小時30分鐘的健康教育課程，內容涵蓋營養、運動及健康生活習慣等主題。
招募對象（需同時符合以下條件）：
年齡60歲或以上
能聽講廣東話
需持續照顧有長期病患的親屬
照顧者負荷指數達7分或以上
沒有經醫生診斷的精神病患或認知問題
沒有嚴重的身體或精神問題
目前並非接受心理治療
過去兩年內未曾參加過正規的靜觀課程
被照顧的親屬並非剛離世
過去三個月內未曾使用抗生素或益生菌
課堂詳情
時間
：暫定於1月中開始，下午時段
地點
：沙田瀝源健康院
形式
：共8節，每週1次，每次1.5小時
兩組參加者均須在課程開始前、結束後，以及結束後3個月，填寫共3次問卷調查，並提供3次糞便樣本。
費用全免

Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!] 🚹🧪🧫🧬🔍!!!注意: 男性特定群組 HPV 病毒篩查   [費用全免] [$400交通津貼]💰💰💰💰 - Department of Surgery
From: Tim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
(參加者太多, 其他組別優先)
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
[
As there are too many participants, other groups will take priority.
]
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.
If you are interested, please register via the link below:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
Suitable applicants will be contacted shortly.
For inquiries, please email:  timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Office of University General Education

大學通識教育基礎課程：2026-27學生活動資助計劃接受申請
各位同學：
自2012年始，大學通識教育基礎課程已在中大全面推行。UGFH和UGFN不知不覺已成為中大人的共同學習經驗。在2026-27學年，大學通識教育基礎課程將繼續推出
學生活動資助計劃
，鼓勵同學們自發設計、推廣及活化與課程相關的活動，在校園內外推廣經典閱讀，鼓勵校內外社群發掘閱讀經典的趣味及當代意義。
本資助計劃接受
個人或小組申請
，以多元形式推廣經典閱讀，包括展覽、讀書會、表演、應用程式、網站及藝術品設計等。申請項目一般須在一年內完成，每個項目最高可獲得港幣3萬元資助。
2026-27
年學生活動資助計劃截止報名日期為
2026
年
11
月
22
日
。
有意申請的同學可參考以下網址，以獲取詳細資料及申請表格：
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/tc/extended-learning/student-activity-fund/
如對本計劃有任何疑問，請電郵至
gef-info@cuhk.edu.hk
或致電3943 3730查詢。我們期待收到你們的申請。
大學通識教育部 通識教育基礎課程　謹啟
General Education Foundation Programme: 2026-27 Student Activity Fund - Call for Application
Dear students,
Since 2012, the General Education (GE) Foundation Programme has been fully launched in CUHK.  Gradually, UGFH and UGFN have become a common learning experience of the CUHK. In 2026-27, the GE Foundation Programme will continue to offer the
Student Activity Fund (SAF)
to encourage student-initiated activities related to the two foundation courses. Through these activities, we hope to promote classics reading by nourishing an enjoyable atmosphere of classics reading in various communities in and out of the campus, and to appreciate the impacts of classics on contemporary society.
The SAF fund accepts applications from
both individuals and groups
. We encourage diversified activities to promote classics reading, including exhibitions, reading groups, performance, APPs, websites and art designs, etc.  Each project should be completed within one year, and could be supported up to HKD 30,000.
The deadline for 2026-27 SAF fund application is 22 November 2026.
If you are interested, please refer to the following website for more details and application forms:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/extended-learning/student-activity-fund/
For enquiries, please contact us by email (
gef-info@cuhk.edu.hk
) or phone (3943 3730). We look forward to hearing from you.
Regards,
General Education Foundation Programme,
Office of University General Education

Announcements
【$100 Subsidy】Recruiting youth aged 12–15 to join an interview on mental health literacy 【$100津貼】誠邀12–15歲青少年參加與精神健康素養相關的個人訪談 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Shirley Lui
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
shirleylui@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學賽馬會公共衞生及基層醫療學院現正進行一項「青少年精神健康素養電腦適應性測驗的開發與驗證」的研究，旨在制訂一份適用於香港青少年的精神健康素養評估量表。研究將安排個人訪談，提問精神健康素養相關問題，並邀請參加者分享其想法與意見。

招募對象
:
12 – 15 歲青少年（需獲家長/監護人同意）
能閱讀中文及可廣東話溝通

答謝安排
:
個人訪談需時約45-60分鐘，成功完成訪問可獲港幣$100元以作答謝。


報名登記連結
:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9oScFBMxsLMtGpU
完成登記後，研究員會聯絡合適的參加者，並安排以面談或線上形式完成一次個人訪談。名額有限！欲報從速！

查詢
:
如有查詢，請聯絡中大職員雷小姐（電話: 2252-8759 / 電郵: shirleylui@cuhk.edu.hk）。
歡迎轉發此訊息給您的家人及朋友！
If you are interested, please click the link below to complete the registration form:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9oScFBMxsLMtGpU
Upon reviewing your registration, our research team will contact eligible participants shortly.
For enquiries, please contact Ms. Lui (Tel: 2252-8759 / Email: shirleylui@cuhk.edu.hk).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Digital Place-Making: Media Technology, Related Population, and Urban-Rural Relations in Japan  - Department of Cultural and Religious Studies
From: Master of Arts Programme in Cultural Management
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
zhuoyueli@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
More people than ever are on the move, and new technologies increasingly shape how we experience the places we live in or leave behind. This talk asks how people make place with the use of digital media technologies such as social media, blockchain, metaverse, and artificial intelligence. It focuses on a group of young and middle-aged urbanites in Japan who came to be identified as the “related population”: city dwellers who never fully move to the countryside, yet stay deeply involved in shrinking rural communities through work, visits, and online connection. I trace where the idea of “related population” came from, explore what these place-makers actually do with technology, and show how they see themselves as belonging to multiple places at once. I argue that today’s urban-rural relations are better understood as cycles rather than one-way moves, but we still need to ask what and who can circulate, how, and with what consequences for the places left behind.
Date
: 10 Nov 2026, Tuesday
Time
: 18:45-20:15
Venue
: KKB 101, Leung Kau Kui Building, CUHK
Guest Speaker: Zhang Jinjin
Jinjin Zhang is a Ph.D. Candidate in the Department of Japanese Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong. Her research examines digital media, sociotechnical innovation, lifestyle migration and mobility, sensory and multi-modal storytelling, and regional revitalization in Japan and China. She previously served as a “Science, Technology, and Society in Asia” Visiting Fellow at the Harvard-Yenching Institute (2025–2026) and as a Japan Foundation Japanese Studies Fellow at Waseda University (2023–2024). Jinjin cares about public humanities and shares her work through blogging, video-making, and podcasting.

Communication Seminar Series - AI and Advertising – New Theoretical Frontiers
Date: 12 November 2026 (Thursday)
Time: 2:30 pm-4:00 pm
Venue: C-Centre (NAH313, Humanities Building, CUHK)
Speaker:Prof. Jisu Huh
Associate Dean & Endowed Chair Professor
College of Liberal Arts
University of Minnesota Twin Cities, USA
Bio:
Dr. Jisu Huh, Ph.D. is a Professor and the Raymond O. Mithun Endowed Chair in Advertising at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities in the USA, where she also serves as the Associate Dean for Research & Graduate Programs in the College of Liberal Arts. A leading voice in her field, Dr. Huh is a past President of the American Academy of Advertising and the current Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of Advertising, the discipline's flagship, top-ranked journal. She is the founder and director of the interdisciplinary Minnesota Computational Advertising Lab (MCAL) (
https://mcal.umn.edu/
). Her cutting-edge research spans computational advertising, AI advertising, consumer trust and information diffusion, social media marketing, and the direct-to-consumer advertising of healthcare products.
Abstract:
Since generative AI’s public release, its rapid adoption across advertising has sparked a surge in scholarly research. While AI enables hyper-personalized content creation at scale, AI-powered search, and agentic shopping, it raises critical questions and concerns. Consumers are increasingly engaging with AI-generated media experiences, blurring the line between the real and the artificial. AI also transforms how consumers search for and process product information, disrupting SEO/SEM strategies. These developments challenge foundational advertising concepts and advertising effect theory. Furthermore, ethical considerations around content ownership, misinformation, and societal impact further underscore the urgent need for thoughtful, responsible frameworks. This seminar examines various topics related to the rise of generative AI in advertising and its implications for advertising practice and scholarship. Through interactive discussion, the speaker will challenge traditional advertising concepts, address key societal risks, and outline a future research agenda to build new theoretical frontiers in the AI era.

中文大學校園面授
本證書課程以參加國家語委普通話水平測試（PSC）為導向，旨在提高學員普通話應用水平，具體表現為：提高學員普通話朗讀能力，掌握普通話水平測試常用詞匯，掌握朗讀規定篇目的方法，讀準字音，讀通作品。同時，提高學員使用普通話所達到的流利程度和規範程度，掌握普通話水平測試應試的技巧，做好測試前的準備；並幫助參加過測試的應試人進一步提升等級，説話時，逐步做到語音標準，語調自然，表達流暢。本證書課程不是零起點課程，學員須具有基礎普通話能力。

title: 【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged under 33 months) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請33個月或以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/30
»
Announcements
【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged under 33 months) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請33個月或以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀3歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 33個月或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿3歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on the gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between the gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is under 33 months old (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 3 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

誠邀您參加一項運動幹預研究!本研究將有助於瞭解您的運動代謝表現並提高您的代謝健康。
研究題目
：比較不同有氧運動訓練對超重或肥胖絕經後女性代謝及循環血液指標影響的隨機對照試驗
親愛的女士：
您好！
隨着年齡增長與絕經後的荷爾蒙變化，您是否覺得體重逐漸增加、脂肪容易囤積，或者開始擔心體脂、血脂等健康指標？香港中文大學體育運動科學系目前正開展一項研究以了解不同有氧運動訓練對絕經後超重或肥胖女性代謝健康的影響。我們誠邀符合條件的華人女性參與，一起通過科學運動重拾健康！
參與本研究，您將免費獲得：
1. 全面身體成分評估：精準檢測體脂率、肌肉量、內臟脂肪等。
2. 專業血液指標檢測：了解您的血脂、血糖等核心代謝指標。
3. 專家級運動能力測試：精準測量您專屬的運動代謝表現，以評估您的體能與代謝反應。
4. 為期 12 週的免費運動指導：由專業研究人員全程跟進，保障運動安全與效果。

我們在尋找這樣的您：
華人女性，且已自然絕經 12 個月或以上（距離最後一次月經少於 6 年）。
體型偏胖（BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² 或 體脂率 > 30%，以實驗室測試為準）。
平時運動較少（每星期少於 150 分鐘中等強度體能活動、少於 75 分鐘劇烈強度體能活動，或二者同等組合）。
過去 3 個月體重相對穩定，且無嚴重運動禁忌（如嚴重心臟病、中風等）。

The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong,
Sports Nutrition and Physical Activity Laboratory,
sincerely invites you to participate in an exercise intervention study! This study will help us understand your exercise metabolic performance and improve your metabolic health.
Study Title
: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing the Effects of Different Aerobic Exercise Training on Metabolic and Circulating Blood Indicators in Postmenopausal Women with overweight or obesity
Dear Madam:
With aging and postmenopausal hormonal changes, do you feel that your weight is gradually increasing, fat is easily accumulated, or you begin to worry about health indicators such as body fat and blood lipids? The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a study to understand the effects of different aerobic exercise training on metabolic health in postmenopausal women with overweight or obesity. We sincerely invite eligible Chinese women to participate and regain health together through scientific exercise!
By participating in this study, you will receive for free:
1. Comprehensive body composition assessment: accurate measurement of body fat percentage, muscle mass, visceral fat, etc.
2. Professional blood indicator testing: understand your core metabolic indicators such as blood lipids and blood glucose.
3. Expert-level exercise capacity test: accurately measure your exercise metabolic performance to evaluate your physical fitness and metabolic response.
4. 12 weeks of free exercise guidance: full follow‑up by professional researchers to ensure exercise safety and effectiveness.
We are looking for:
1. Chinese women who have been naturally postmenopausal for 12 months or more (less than 6 years since the last menstrual period).
2. Are overweight or obese (BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² or body fat percentage > 30%; will be confirmed by laboratory testing).
3. Are usually physically inactive (less than 150 minutes of moderate‑intensity physical activity, less than 75 minutes of vigorous‑intensity physical activity per week, or an equivalent combination).
4. Have had relatively stable body weight in the past 3 months, and have no serious contraindications to exercise (e.g., severe heart disease, stroke, etc.).
⏳ What do you need to do? (3 assessments + 12‑week intervention training)
This study lasts 12 weeks. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to a
control group
,
aerobic
exercise group A,
or
aerobic exercise group B
. During the period, you will need to visit the laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong for 3 assessments, including: questionnaire surveys, fasting venous blood draw, finger‑prick blood sampling, body composition measurement, and exercise metabolic testing. To reduce discomfort during testing, the exercise metabolic test will be conducted separately from other health tests. Throughout the study, you will need to come to the laboratory
6 times.
12‑week intervention training: 3 times per week, 40‑70 minutes per session, for 12 weeks.
Upon completion of the study, you will receive a HK$150 shopping voucher and a health report.
Trial location: G02 Office, Ground Floor, Kwok Sports Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Register now / Enquire:
Places are limited, first‑come, first‑served! You can click the link below to register:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfZKjSc55Ov13iAjw_GAGkFIbINsXc9rH1ePEYg6CWrU5w5Ew/viewform?usp=header
If you have any questions, please contact the research team:
Study coordinator: Ms. He (WhatsApp: +852 5984 8824)
Supervising professor: Prof. Stephen Heung-sang WONG (Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Wishing you good health!
Research Team
Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Respectfully

Better Gut, Better Sleep? Gut-Brain Study | Earn up to HKD 500  「腸」通無阻，瞓得更好？「腸·腦」研究 | 最高可獲 HKD 500 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Michael Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
tsztsunng@cuhk.edu.hk

近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼

[網址連結:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders
What you will do:
Complete questionnaires and a brief interview
Undergo a sleep assessment
Record a 2-week bowel diary
Complete a colonic transit time test
Collect one stool sample

All assessments are free of charge.

The Practice of New Museology in Humanistic Buddhism: Venerable Master Hsing Yun’s Museum Vision 【Hybrid Lecture】 人間佛教的新博物館學實踐:星雲大師的博物館情懷 - Centre for the Study of Humanistic Buddhism
From: 人間佛教研究中心 Centre for the Study of Humanistic Buddhism
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cshb@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【精彩上線｜紀念星雲大師百歲誕辰系列講座】
為紀念星雲大師百歲誕辰，香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心與佛學研究中心聯合舉辦 「人間佛教的文本、行跡與時代開展」 系列講座。我們特別邀請了宗教學、文學、哲學、出版、媒體與博物館學等領域的頂尖專家學者，帶來 9 場重磅專題演講！內容橫跨跨跨文化對話、文學考察、媒體實踐到新博物館學，從多元視角深化對星雲大師思想的理解。本次系列講座全面開放線上參與，歡迎大眾踴躍共霑法益。
題目：
人間佛教的新博物館學實踐:星雲大師的博物館情懷
時間：11月4日 | 週三 10:00 - 12:00
講者：張譽騰教授 | 國立台南藝術大學博物館學研究所兼任教授
主持：陳劍鍠教授 | 香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心主任
形式：現場講座 & ZOOM網絡會議
地點：香港中文大學馮景禧樓 & 會議ID: 964 5779 7423，密碼: 999999
報名：https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741301
演講簡介：
「人間佛教」主張佛法不離世間，強調將佛法落實在日常生活，服務社會，讓佛教從山林走入社會，此正與新博物館學訴求遙相呼應。星雲大師是宗教開創者，但很少人知道他在博物館方面也建樹良多，疊有新意。本講座將從三個面向探討大師在新博物館學的成就:
一、從生態博物館角度說明整座佛光山其實就是一座無牆博物館。
二、從博物館與科技、社區和永續三個層次，說明佛陀紀念館成立迄今，如何與時俱進，踐行新博物館學理念。
三、從佛光山核心館與衛星館發展策略談佛光緣美術館群如何與在地道場結合，將佛光山能量有效輻射出去。
"Humanistic Buddhism" advocates that the Buddha-Dharma is not separate from the world, emphasizing the implementation of Buddhist teachings in daily life, serving society, and guiding Buddhism from isolated mountains into secular society. This philosophy echoes the core pursuits of "New Museology."
While Venerable Master Hsing Yun is widely recognized as a religious pioneer, few are aware of his profound achievements and innovative ideas in the field of museum studies.This presentation will explore the Master’s achievements in New Museology through three main dimensions:
1. The Ecomuseum Perspective: Illustrating how the entirety of Fo Guang Shan functions as a "Museum without Walls."
2. Technology, Community, and Sustainability: Examining how the Fo Guang Shan Buddha Museum has kept pace with the times since its inception, putting the principles of New Museology into practice.
3. Core and Satellite Museum Development Strategy: Discussing how the Fo Guang Yuan Art Galleries integrate with local Buddhist centers (dojos) to effectively radiate Fo Guang Shan's energy outward.
嘉賓簡介：
張譽騰教授，畢業於國立台灣大學動物學系，1992年獲得英國萊斯特大學(University of Leicester)博物館學博士。曾任國立台南藝術大學博物館學研究所教授和文博學院院長、行政院文化建設委員會政務副主委、國立歷史博物館館長、中華民國博物館學會理事長、佛光大學講座教授。主要學術著作有: 《當代博物館探索》、《博物館大勢觀察》、《生態博物館:一個文化運動的興起》。現為國立台南藝術大學博物館學研究所兼任教授，並擔任佛光山顧問與學術委員會委員。

香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期九個月，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病 (例如:心臟病或中風等重大併發症)
沒有服用中藥
身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
患糖尿病6 年或以下
目前飲食控制或用2種或以下口服糖尿藥 [例如metformin（品牌藥名：Glucophage）或/及 gliclazide（品牌藥名：Diamicron）]
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，但具備以下其中一項風險因素，我們會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）作篩查
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等

Announcements
[Tired of Nightmares and Insomnia?] Join Our Free Online Treatment Study 【成日發惡夢又瞓唔著？】全新網上治療研究，6周助你重拾安睡 - Department of psychiatry
From: Reyane Ao
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
您是否正飽受
惡夢
與
失眠
的雙重困擾，覺得身心俱疲？
反覆的惡夢有機會加劇失眠問題，導致日頭精神大打折扣。
我們誠邀您參與一項
【網上認知行為療法治療噩夢與失眠共病】臨床研究
。本研究旨在評估一項手機應用程式的自助式網上療程，學習有效改善睡眠、減少惡夢的心理療法。
您的參與不僅有機會能幫助自己重獲優質睡眠，更能推動睡眠醫學的發展，為有同樣困擾的人士帶來新的證據。

我們正在招募
年齡介乎 18 至 64 歲
同時受失眠及惡夢問題困擾
能閱讀繁體中文並以粵語溝通

研究內容包括
臨床訪談及問卷篩查
為期6周網上認知行為治療課程（每週約20-30分鐘課程）
完成治療後的問卷和跟進評估
佩戴睡眠手錶

參與方法
如有興趣，請點擊以下連結，花1-2分鐘填寫篩選問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dbt7HLJzt16miEK

重要提示
初步符合條件者，我們的研究團隊將在
一個月
內與您聯繫，進行後續評估並詳細說明研究詳情。若未獲通知，暫不符合本次招募範圍，敬請諒解。

查詢及聯絡
如有任何疑問，歡迎通過以下方式聯繫研究團隊：
WhatsApp/電話：6763 1454
電郵：
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
您提供的所有資料將會嚴格保密，僅供本研究使用。
歡迎將此信息轉發
給可能有需要的人士。感謝您的關注與支持！
Dear Sir/Madam,
Are you struggling with both nightmares and insomnia, feeling mentally and physically exhausted?
Recurring nightmares can make insomnia even worse, severely affecting your sleep quality and leaving you drained during the day.​
We invite you to take part in a clinical study on an
online cognitive behavioural therapy program for co-occurring nightmares and insomnia
. This study aims to evaluate an innovative mobile application–based treatment. Through this free and convenient self-help online program, you can learn evidence-based psychological techniques to improve your sleep and reduce nightmares.​
Your participation not only offers you a chance to achieve better sleep but also contributes to advancing sleep medicine, helping to build new evidence for others facing similar challenges.
Who we are recruiting
​
Aged between 18 and 64
Experiencing both insomnia and recurrent nightmares
Able to read Traditional Chinese and communicate in Cantonese​
What the study involves
​
Clinical interview and screening questionnaires
A 6-week online cognitive behavioural therapy program (requiring approximately 20-30 minutes per week)
Post-treatment questionnaires and follow-up assessments​
Wearing a research-grade sleep monitoring device (activity level tracker)
How to Participate
If you are interested, please click the link below to complete a brief screening questionnaire:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dbt7HLJzt16miEK
Important Note
Only applicants who preliminarily meet the eligibility criteria will be contacted by our research team within one month for further assessment and a detailed study explanation. We appreciate your understanding.
Enquiries & Contact
For any questions, please feel free to contact our research team, via:
WhatsApp/Phone: 6763 1454
Email: sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
All information you provide will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for research purposes.
Please feel free to share this opportunity
with anyone who might benefit. Thank you for your interest and support!
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

內與您聯繫，進行後續評估並詳細說明研究詳情。若未獲通知，暫不符合本次招募範圍，敬請諒解。

查詢及聯絡
如有任何疑問，歡迎通過以下方式聯繫研究團隊：
WhatsApp/電話：6763 1454
電郵：
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
您提供的所有資料將會嚴格保密，僅供本研究使用。
歡迎將此信息轉發
給可能有需要的人士。感謝您的關注與支持！
Dear Sir/Madam,
Are you struggling with both nightmares and insomnia, feeling mentally and physically exhausted?
Recurring nightmares can make insomnia even worse, severely affecting your sleep quality and leaving you drained during the day.​
We invite you to take part in a clinical study on an
online cognitive behavioural therapy program for co-occurring nightmares and insomnia
. This study aims to evaluate an innovative mobile application–based treatment. Through this free and convenient self-help online program, you can learn evidence-based psychological techniques to improve your sleep and reduce nightmares.​
Your participation not only offers you a chance to achieve better sleep but also contributes to advancing sleep medicine, helping to build new evidence for others facing similar challenges.
Who we are recruiting
​
Aged between 18 and 64
Experiencing both insomnia and recurrent nightmares
Able to read Traditional Chinese and communicate in Cantonese​
What the study involves
​
Clinical interview and screening questionnaires
A 6-week online cognitive behavioural therapy program (requiring approximately 20-30 minutes per week)
Post-treatment questionnaires and follow-up assessments​
Wearing a research-grade sleep monitoring device (activity level tracker)
How to Participate
If you are interested, please click the link below to complete a brief screening questionnaire:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dbt7HLJzt16miEK
Important Note
Only applicants who preliminarily meet the eligibility criteria will be contacted by our research team within one month for further assessment and a detailed study explanation. We appreciate your understanding.
Enquiries & Contact
For any questions, please feel free to contact our research team, via:
WhatsApp/Phone: 6763 1454
Email: sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
All information you provide will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for research purposes.
Please feel free to share this opportunity
with anyone who might benefit. Thank you for your interest and support!

CUHK Jockey Club AI for the Future Project
Funded by The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust, CUHK Jockey Club AI for the Future Project (“
the Project
”) brings together the strong expertise of CUHK Faculties of Engineering and Education. The Project’s objective is to create a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) curriculum, a sustainable AI education model, with relevant supporting infrastructure to establish a conducive ecosystem in AI education for Hong Kong’s secondary schools.
About Toolkit Team
To facilitate teachers’ teaching and students’ learning AI, the Toolkit Team is responsible for developing AI toolkits to support the Project’s AI Curriculum. The Toolkit team is also responsible for managing the Project’s AI Education and Exploration Lab (“the Lab”) at CUHK, as well as to develop AI-related demonstrations to be exhibited at the Lab and offer AI educational activities such as workshops and courses.
The Project team is looking for part-time students focusing on
web application
. Job responsibilities and requirements are as follows:
No. of Vacancies:
5
Salary:
HKD 67 per hour
Working Hours:
A minimum of 4 hours/ week and maximum 17 hours/ week
Working Location:
Rm 902, 9/F, William M. W. Mong Engineering Building (ERB), CUHK
OR
HKSTP
Job Descriptions
To assist in developing web applications related to AI education and AI toolkits;
To work with designers to develop websites’ user interface;
To conduct research and experiments on web technologies and frameworks;
To document code and maintain code repositories; and
To handle any ad hoc duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Study Year Requirements
Full-time undergraduate students
Full-time postgraduate students
Other Requirements
Basic knowledge of JavaScript/ HTML/ CSS;
Basic knowledge of using Git for project version management;
Experience in front-end development, particularly responsive web design/UI/UX design would be a plus;
Possess a good track record in technical development; and
Responsible, willingness to learn and able to work independently.
(Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview)
Please submit your CV and state the position(s) that you want to apply by email to Miss. Rachel CHEN (rachelchen@cuhk.edu.hk) by 23:59, 06 Nov 2026 (Fri).

From: Amber Lam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ics-activities@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
You are cordially invited to attend a public lecture organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies (ICS) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong on next Thursday, 29 October 2026.
It is our honour to welcome Prof. Ping WANG, ICS Visiting Fellowship visiting scholar from Department of Asian Languages and Literature at the University of Washington, to deliver a talk on the topic: "Untranslating the Poet-Transcendent: Li Bo (701–762) Between Cosmology and Equivalence".
Abstract:
Large language models now translate between languages in seconds, reviving an old anxiety: is translation a solved problem? This talk argues that for understanding a culture, fluency was never the difficulty. Taking the great Tang poet Li Bo as its case, it follows a singularly iconic word, xian 仙, the term behind his epithet "poet-transcendent," as it passes into English. In medieval China, a xian was not merely a being who does not die; a xian held rank and office in a celestial bureaucracy, and could be demoted from it. To render Li Bo a "banished immortal" keeps the exile but quietly drops that cosmic officialdom, leaving behind a familiar romantic genius. For a century "immortal" was the dominant English choice, canonized in dictionaries and anthologies until it seemed self-evident. Machine translation, trained on that same archive, reproduces the reduction as its frictionless default, laying bare how thoroughly it saturated the record. The question, then, is not whether cultures can be translated, but how a concept, precisely by resisting translation, becomes a shared medium for thinking transcendence.
Speaker:
Ping Wang is Professor in the Department of Asian Languages and Literature at the University of Washington, where she teaches classical Chinese literature and researches the history of Chinese poetry. She has previously held faculty positions at the University of Wisconsin and Princeton University, prior to joining the University of Washington.
Professor Wang's scholarship bridges Western sinology, translation studies, traditional Chinese classical learning, and contemporary critical theory. She has published numerous articles and is the author of
The Age of Courtly Writing: Wen xuan Compiler Xiao Tong (501-531) and His Circle
and
The Poetic Way of Xie Lingyun
, the latter of which examines the significance of landscape poetry (shanshui shi) in Chinese literary history.
Her honors include a research membership at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, a special Andrew W. Mellon Foundation grant for international collaborative research, and a research fellowship from the Simpson Center for the Humanities at the University of Washington. In 2017, she was invited to lecture at the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia, and she is currently a resident fellow of the Institute of Chinese Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Morningside College is proud to host a public conversation with South Korean author Kim Choyeop and translator-author Anton Hur on
If We Cannot Go at the Speed of Light
(2026), a landmark collection of Korean speculative fiction that brings together space travel, memory, grief, technology, and the ethics of care. Designed for a broad university/public audience, this event uses the book as a springboard into urgent contemporary questions: What makes us human? Can technology deepen empathy—or merely repackage loneliness? What do we owe the dead, the vulnerable, and one another in increasingly mediated futures? Accessible to readers beyond science fiction, the conversation will also explore how literary translation carries tone, ambiguity, and conceptual complexity across languages.

: “

”
As
CUHK Graduate School
celebrates its
60th Anniversary
, we are not only reflecting on six decades of excellence, innovation, and impact, but also looking ahead to the future of education in an increasingly AI-driven world.
To mark this milestone, we are pleased to invite you to join us on 6 November 2026 (Fri) for a series of celebration activities
,
including our annual signature event, the
Graduate School Seminar 202
6:
“
AI in Education
”
, a
networking session
bringing together speakers, students, and alumni from diverse backgrounds and disciplines, as well as a
mini exhibition
showcasing the Graduate School’s history and achievements.
Jointly organised by the CUHK Graduate School and the Federation of Graduate School Alumni Associations (FGSAA), the
Graduate School Seminar 2026: "AI in Education"
presents a forward-looking dialogue on how artificial intelligence is transforming teaching and learning, research, and graduate education.
We are honoured to welcome three distinguished speakers who will share their insights on the evolving role of AI in education in keynote speeches and panel discussion:

"From Knowledge to Discovery: AI and the Future of Graduate Education"
Professor Irwin KING
- Pro-Vice-Chancellor / Vice-President (Education)
- Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering

Blueprint for Digital Education Development in Primary and Secondary Schools
"

- Chairman, Hong Kong Education City
- Graduate of
@CUHK MBA

- Certified AI Trainer of United Nations University
- Graduate of
@CUHK EMBA

- Executive Director, Hong Kong Education City
- Graduate of
@CUHK EMBA
Panelist

networking session with refreshments
, providing an opportunity for alumni, students, academics, and professionals to connect, exchange ideas, and explore new collaborations.

title: [30 Oct Anthropology Friday Seminar] Hui Lok Hang, "Emotional Connection in Contemporary Japan: An Example from the Revitalisation of Bridal Curtains"

[30 Oct Anthropology Friday Seminar] Hui Lok Hang, "Emotional Connection in Contemporary Japan: An Example from the Revitalisation of Bridal Curtains"  - Anthropology
From: M.W.Leung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
anthropology@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear all,
You are cordially invited to join a talk on 30 October, in which Dr. Hui Lok Hang will discuss how the revitalisation of bridal curtains reflects changing expectations for the expression of affection in close relationships in Japan.
Title: Emotional Connection in Contemporary Japan: An Example from the Revitalisation of Bridal Curtains
Speaker: Hui Lok Hang (Independent Researcher)
Date: Friday 30 October, 2026
Time: 1:00-2:30pm
Mode: In-person
Venue: Room 114, Humanities Building, New Asia College, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Look forward to seeing you at the Friday Seminar!
Regards,
Department of Anthropology, CUHK
Abstract:
This paper traces the revitalisation of hanayome noren to examine changing expressions of affection and care in family and community relationships in contemporary Japan. Hanayome noren are bridal curtains traditionally included in wedding trousseaus in Japan's Hokuriku region. Usually commissioned by the bride's parents, the curtain was hung at the entrance to the Buddhist altar room in the groom’s home during the wedding. Passing beneath it marked the bride’s entry into the household. After the wedding, the curtain was stored away and seldom displayed again. The custom declined as weddings increasingly took place at commercial venues. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork on the Noto Peninsula, this study focuses on two developments: an exhibition of stored curtains and new personalised designs incorporating childhood memories and hometown landscapes. The exhibition helped shopkeepers' wives on the same shopping street develop friendships. Through the creation and use of personalised curtains, parents and married daughters expressed care for one another despite living apart. The paper situates these developments within changing expectations of close relationships in Japan. As prescribed family and community roles become less binding, bonds based on experienced affection gain importance. At the same time, affection within both natal and marital relationships is increasingly expected to be communicated and demonstrated explicitly. The example of bridal curtain revitalisation shows how people respond to these expectations by reworking an inherited wedding custom.
Bio:
HUI Lok Hang specialises in material culture and the anthropology of Japan. He obtained his PhD in Anthropology from University College London. His doctoral research examined how families live with butsudan (Buddhist home altars) in rural Japan. It shows how the material arrangements and everyday rhythms surrounding these altars create an atmosphere of care that sustains interactions between the living and the dead and connects households with relatives, neighbours and temples. He received his MPhil from The Chinese University of Hong Kong, where his research examined the social life of Japanese candles (warōsoku).

中大兒科過敏組將籌辦「中大過敏週2026」以加強市民對過敏性疾病的教育，並以「
濕疹及食物過敏的管理與預防新進展
」為主題
我們誠邀您參加以下中大過敏週活動⏬⏬

過敏工作坊
此工作坊專為患有過敏症人士、過敏病童的家長及幼兒園、幼稚園和小學教職員而設。

CUHK Paediatric Allergy Team
is organizing
CU Allergy Week 2026
to enhance public awareness and education on allergic diseases, with the theme:

"Advances in Management and Prevention of Eczema and Food Allergy"
We warmly invite you to join the following CU Allergy Week activities ⏬⏬

Allergy Workshops
This workshop is designed for individuals living with allergic conditions, parents of children with allergies, as well as teaching and support staff from nurseries, kindergartens, and primary schools.
Date:
31 October 2026 (Saturday)
Session Times:
13:00-13:45 / 14:00-14:45 (45 minutes per session)
This year's workshop will cover two topics:
Eczema and Anaphylaxis
Asthma and Allergic Rhinitis

A Certificate of Attendance will be awarded to all participants.

Join paediatric consultants from

, professors from the

• How to Select Emollients for Eczema Patients?
• Introduction to Allergy Diagnosis

• Drug Allergy: Facts and Myths

15:20-17:00

Free of charge (advance registration required)

https://registration.cuallergyweek2026.com/register

[Register Now!] [6 NOV] Areas of Excellence (AoE) Use data to transform diabetes care and patient lives Live Webinar Series (2026-2027)  - Hong Kong Institute of Diabetes and Obesity
From: LAU Wing Man
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hkido@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear All,
You’re cordially invited to join
Areas of Excellence (AoE)
Use data to transform diabetes care and patient lives
Live Webinar Series (2026-2027)
with the details below:
Join us for the
Areas of Excellence (AoE) Live Webinar Series (2026-2027)
which we have invited global leaders and experts in biomedical-psychosocial-behavioral science to share the latest knowledge in epidemiology, diagnosis, prevention and treatment from early to late stage in pursuit of the vision of the Lancet Commission Report on diabetes.
In this monthly webinar, we have invited experts to discuss the challenges and opportunities of implementing data-driven diabetes prevention and care and explore opportunities of setting a Global Diabetes Register using the JADE Platform in our common goal of making healthcare sustainable and helping people live a healthy and better life.
Learning objectives
Understand what, why, how, by whom and for whom of setting up diabetes registers
Set up a network of collaborators to establish a multicounty JADE Register with automatic data anonymization, using common protocol to gather real world evidence, share best practices and improve quality of care
Enable researchers and care providers to work collectively to define the clinical profiles of their population, benchmark their care performance, establish biobanks and implement pragmatic clinical studies to address unmet needs
About the speaker
About the speaker
Professor Calvin Ke
Assistant Professor of Medicine and Institute of Health Policy, Management and Evaluation, University of Toronto, Canada
Professor Andrea Luk
Professor, Department of Medicine and Therapeutics, Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, HKSAR, China
Date & time: 6 November 2026 (Friday) | 17:00-18:00 HKT (UTC+8)
Online: via Zoom — link provided upon registration
Register
HERE
To learn more, please visit
HERE
Don’t miss this opportunity for setting up the JADE Register at your institution with access to the portal for a trial period to explore feasibility.
Acknowledgement of the RGC Area of Excellence Scheme on Diabetes (AoE/M-401/24-R).

仰望星空，探索極致宇宙 ——「院士進校園」天文物理學名師講堂
Distinguished Academician Lecture Series: Gaze at the Stars, Explore the Extreme Universe
本次「院士進校園」講堂由中國科學院紫金山天文台與香港中文大學聯合舉辦，特邀崔向群院士、林海青院士及史生才院士蒞臨中大。活動立足香港國際交流樞紐與科研協同優勢，全方位展示國家在光學觀測、理論計算及太赫茲探測等天文物理前沿領域的硬核實力。三位名師將帶領青年學子與天文同好穿透星際塵埃，探索極限物理法則，在思想碰撞中拓展學術視野、啟迪科研志趣！
【活動詳情 Event Details】
日期 Date：
2026年11月13日（星期五）/ 13 November 2026 (Friday)
時間 Time：
下午 3:00 – 5:45 (3:00 PM – 5:45 PM)
地點 Venue：
香港中文大學鄭裕彤樓鄭家純國際會議中心1樓（地下）LT1B, G/F, Cheng Yu Tung Building (CYT), CUHK
主辦機構 Organizers：
中國科學院紫金山天文台、香港中文大學
承辦單位 Co-organizers：
香港中文大學香港極地科學創新中心、粵港澳大灣區發展辦公室、深圳研究院
語言 Language：
普通話 (Putonghua)
【主講嘉賓 Keynote Speakers】
崔向群 院士 (Academician XIANGQUN CUI)
中國科學院院士、南京天文光學技術研究所研究員
國家重大科技基礎設施大天區面積多目標光纖光譜望遠鏡（LAMOST）總工程師
林海青 院士 (Academician HAIQING LIN)
中國科學院院士、浙江大學物理學院院長
凝聚態物理與計算物理知名專家

中國科學院院士、紫金山天文台研究員
太赫茲超導探測技術專家、國家深空與天文探測載荷領域領軍學者

New Programme Launch: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) Essentials (Level 1-Stage 1)
Are you looking to deepen your mindfulness practice or integrate evidence-based mindfulness into your professional work? The CUHK Thomas Jing Centre for Mindfulness Research and Training is proud to announce the upcoming MBSR Essentials Programme!
MBSR Essentials is the foundational step in the MBSR Teacher Training Pathway. It offers an experiential exploration of the MBSR curriculum, cultivating core teaching competencies and deep personal understanding from the inside out.
Ideal For:
• Aspiring qualified MBSR teachers and introductory workshop facilitators
• Helping professionals (counsellors, therapists, social workers, educators, healthcare practitioners)
• Anyone wishing to deepen their mindfulness understanding and personal practice
Programme Details:
• Dates: 21 Feb 2027 – 25 Apr 2027 (2 months | 11 sessions)
• Lead Trainer: Mr. Kevin Fong (Co-founder, ATINAT Institute of Mindfulness Training)

• Language: Taught in Cantonese (with English materials)
• Fee: HKD 22,500
• Application Deadline: 31 Dec 2026 (Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and will close once all places are filled or on the deadline, whichever comes first. Early application is encouraged.)

bodyText:

Announcements
Microsoft Copilot Chat Tips Ace Your Data Assignments — Instant Analysis  - ITSC
From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Got an Excel/CSV file and no idea what to do with it? Whether it's a stats class or lab report —
Copilot
can
analyze your data, generate charts, and explain the results
like a personal data scientist.
Prompt 1 — copy & paste it!
Upload & explore
"I've uploaded my dataset. Give me: 1) A summary of what this data contains 2) Key statistics for numeric columns 3) Interesting patterns or outliers 4) 3 questions this data could answer."
Prompt 2 — keep the conversation going!
Visualize it
"Create a bar chart comparing [column A] across [column B]. Also create a line chart showing the trend over time. Use clear labels, a legend, and a title. Explain what each chart reveals."
Prompt 3 — go advanced!
Advanced analysis
"Run a correlation analysis between [variable 1] and [variable 2]. Create a scatter plot with a trend line. Is the correlation significant? What does this mean? How would I report this in a paper?"
Why this works:
Copilot doesn't just crunch numbers — it explains results in language you can actually use in your assignments!

Bonus tip:

bodyText:

Professional Certificate in Mindfulness Facilitator Training Programme  - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Emily Leung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
emilyleung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Integrating Mindfulness into Professional Practice: A Mindfulness Facilitator Training
Are you a professional in healthcare, social work, psychology, or education who wants to integrate mindfulness into your service, but feels unsure about how to introduce it safely and flexibly?
Many frontline practitioners have learned approaches that incorporate mindfulness (such as ACT or DBT), but due to limited course hours, may feel their core grasp of mindfulness needs a deeper, more solid foundation.
Taught in Cantonese, this training is designed specifically for professionals working with adult service users. It moves beyond standard 8-week group training to focus on practical 1-on-1 applications, short workshops, and experiential creative tools!
3 Programme Highlights:
Creative & Diverse Modalities: Go beyond foundational practices with Mindful Tea Drinking, Mindful Clay, and Mindful Jar creation—engaging ways to introduce mindfulness to your clients.
Tailored for Helping Contexts: Learn to guide mindfulness safely, ethically, and adaptively within individual counseling or group sessions.
Comprehensive Support System: Includes 6 months of structured learning, a 3-day silent retreat, small-group tutorials, and post-course practice supervision.
Trainer: Prof. Stanley Chan
• Adjunct Assistant Professor, JC School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK
• Educational Psychologist (HKDEP Registered)
• Oxford Mindfulness Foundation (OMF) Certified Trainer
• Mindfulness Network (UK) Approved Supervisor
Course Schedule & Logistics
Stage 1: Theory & Core Skills (Location: D' Hub, Prince Edward)
• Full-Day Sessions (09:30 – 18:30):
Dec 19, 2026 (Sat) | Jan 2, Jan 16, Jan 30, Jan 31 (Sun), Feb 13, 2027 (Sat)
• 1st Group Tutorial (1.5 hrs/group): March 7, 2027 (Sun)
Stage 2: 3-Day Silent Retreat (Non-overnight, Venue TBC)
• Full-Day Retreat (09:30 – 18:30 TBC): March 26–28, 2027 (Easter Holiday, Fri–Sun)
• 2nd Group Tutorial (1.5 hrs/group): April 10, 2027 (Sat)
Stage 3: Practice & Integration (Location: D' Hub, Prince Edward)
• Full-Day Sessions (09:30 – 18:30):
April 24, May 1, May 8, 2027 (Sat)
• 3rd Group Tutorial (1.5 hrs/group): May 22 & May 29, 2027 (mornings)
Post-Course Supervision Stage:
• 2 sessions of small group practice supervision (1.5 hrs each) within 30–90 days following Stage 3.
Entry Requirements:
1. Mindfulness Foundation: Completion of an 8-week mindfulness course (MBCT, MBCT-L, or MBSR) by an accredited organization/teacher.
2. Professional Qualification: Bachelor’s degree in healthcare, health, or social services with active membership in a regulated local professional body (e.g., Registered Social Worker, Educational/Clinical Psychologist, Registered Nurse).
3. Silent Retreat Experience: Completion of one 5-7 day or two 3-day overnight silent retreats. (Note: Applicants currently pending retreat completion may still apply provided they commit to fulfilling it before completing this training.)
Fees:
• Application Fee: HKD $300
• Tuition Fee: HKD $29,500
Application Deadline: 16 November 2026 (Admissions on a rolling basis—early submission is strongly encouraged!)

bodyText:

Announcements
Call for nominations for SCGE Exemplary Teaching Award in General Education 2026  - Office of University General Education
From: Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ouge@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear Members of the CUHK Community,
We are pleased to announce that nominations for the Exemplary Teaching Award in General Education 2026 are now open.  This Award is presented annually to recognize teachers for their outstanding contributions to teaching and learning in General Education (GE). Departments, Faculties, Programmes of Study, Colleges, GE teachers, and undergraduate students are welcome to submit nominations.
Nominees should hold a full-time appointment.  All nominations, upon endorsement by heads of the respective units, will be reviewed by SCGE and its Standing Committee, with primary consideration given to evidence of sustained excellence in the nominee’s contributions to GE.  Relevant supporting documentation, including records of the nominee’s contributions to GE during the past two academic years (i.e. 2024-25 and 2025-26 for the current call) should be submitted to facilitate the evaluation.  Contributions to teaching and learning will be evaluated based on the following objectives of the CUHK GE Programme and expectations of GE courses:
Objectives of CUHK GE Programme:
Provide a broad intellectual perspective and to instill an understanding of the values of different academic disciplines;
Develop sensitivity to the common concerns of human existence especially from the perspective of the Chinese culture;
Help students develop their own judgment and sense of values;
Cultivate awareness of the connections among different fields of knowledge; to develop the potentiality for integrating different fields of knowledge as needed; and
Equip students with life-long learning capacities especially through understanding of the connections between academic pursuits and life experience.
Expectations of GE courses:
GE courses should be at the same intellectual level as major courses, and should carry the same workload as major courses with the same number of units.
Upon receipt of each nomination, the Office of University General Education (OUGE), as the secretariat of SCGE, will contact the nominee concerned directly for the required supporting materials.  More information about the Award can be found on the OUGE website:
https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/oge/eta
.  Nominations should be made through the
online nomination form
by 16 November 2026.
For any inquiries, feel free to contact us at
ouge@cuhk.edu.hk
or call us at 3943 7075.
Thank you for helping us recognize the exceptional educators who contribute to our community.
Best regards,
Office of University General Education

「佛學研究文學碩士」
2027-28
課程現正接受申請 (2027年9月入學)
~~~
凝視人間，悲智雙運
~~~
課程使命與目標
為致力於推展佛教教育及佛學研究，香港中文大學「文化及宗教研究系」與「人間佛教研究中心」合辦此課程，培育有志於佛學研究之人士，理解漢傳佛教之整體歷史脈絡及各個學派、宗派之思想理論，既而繼續深研、拓展其佛學研究之深度與廣度，為學生提供專業、系統而全面的佛學研究訓練，包括經典文本、哲學思想、歷史文化、倫理道德等各方面研究，重視長時段之歷時性探討，延及當代社會議題之討論，貫穿古今，促進亞洲多元的佛教歷史文化之學習。
課程範圍
範圍一：中國佛教                   範圍二：佛教與中國文化
範圍三：佛教與社會               範圍四：語言課程

2027-28 Programme of Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies is now OPEN for Applications
Our motto: Seeing Humanity with Compassion and Wisdom
Mission and Objectives
To promote Buddhist studies, the Department of Cultural and Religious Studies (CRS) and the Center for the Study of Humanistic Buddhism (CSHB) launch a programme of “Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies”. The programme promotes an understanding of the Mahāyāna Buddhism in its historical context and teachings and thoughts of its different schools. It also emphasizes a depth and breadth of understanding and a life-long learning of the Buddhist tradition. It adopts a multi-disciplinary approach that studies the Buddhist tradition from textual, philosophical, historical and ethical perspectives. It promotes an academic study of Buddhism that studies Buddhism in its many forms within its Asian historical and cultural context. It will also engage students in a discussion of contemporary social issues. It aspires to nurture scholars and provides them with the professional and comprehensive training in Asian holistic Buddhist studies.
Areas of Study
Area 1: Chinese Buddhism                   Area 2: Buddhism and Chinese Culture
Area 3: Buddhism and Society              Area 4: Language Courses

Please check form the webpage of the Graduate School:

28 February 2027 (Priority round)

title: Recruiting women with gestational diabetes - 4 free postpartum body check ups (current or within 12 weeks postpartum) 招募妊娠糖尿病媽媽-4 次免費產後身體檢查 (包括現時及過去12週已生產的)
bodyText:

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students

2026/10/23
»
Announcements
Recruiting women with gestational diabetes - 4 free postpartum body check ups (current or within 12 weeks postpartum)  招募妊娠糖尿病媽媽-4 次免費產後身體檢查 (包括現時及過去12週已生產的) - Dept of Medicine and Therapeutics - Diabetes & Endocrine Research Centre
From: AOE GDM
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
kayancheung001@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
⭐⭐⭐誠邀各位參與香港妊娠糖尿病登記冊⭐⭐⭐

招募對象：
患有妊娠糖尿的媽媽 (現時或已生產的12週内）
懷單胞胎
18-50 歲
沒有正在服用類固醇
沒有患上不受控的甲狀腺疾病
沒有於妊娠期外確診糖尿病
沒有正參與其他降體重或生活干預的計劃/研究
在懷孕以外的期間，服用降血糖或控制體重藥物

背景

曾患有妊娠糖尿病既媽媽：
將來患上二型糖尿病既風險
高達7倍
患有高血壓，脂肪肝及其他心血管疾病風險
較高
小朋友於7歲時出現糖尿病，超重/肥胖或高血壓的機會率亦比一般小朋友
高

問題

香港對於該如何在產後跟進患有妊娠糖尿病的婦女，尚無標準建議。
雖然妊娠糖尿病婦女患有高血壓、血脂異常和肥胖等其他代謝問題的風險較高，但這些問題在妊娠糖尿病後並不會有常規監測。

研究內容 (費用全免)

我們將為媽媽提供4次身體檢查 (3 年）：
第1次: 在產後第6-12週
第2次: 1年後
第3次: 2年後
第4次: 3年後

地點：
香港中文大學醫院

年度回訪内容包括

口服葡萄糖耐量試驗 - 糖水測試
血液檢查 （血糖，血脂，肝功能，腎功能）
Fibroscan 肝臟掃描
Skin AGEs 測試 - 心血管疾病風險
血壓心跳及基本身體檢查 （身高，體重，腰圍，臀圍，Inbody - 脂肪比例）
問卷 (了解身體狀況，家族病史，飲食及運動習慣，哺育習慣等等）
第三年將邀請小朋友回來量度皮下脂肪和口腔拭子
提供免費電子平臺以接收健康資訊
此外，部分高風險的參加者將獲邀參加一個為期3年的糖尿病預防計劃，並有機會接受註冊營養師和運動教練一對一的飲食和運動指導，並會獲發運動記錄手錶和連續血糖監測儀。

如有興趣，請透過以下方式報名：
1. https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_es7l8ryzLKFuXie
2. 掃描QR code
3. Whatsapp +852 6743 9107
如有查詢歡迎Whatsapp +852 6743 9107
再次多謝你對本研究的興趣謝謝
⭐⭐⭐ You’re invited to join the Hong Kong Gestational Diabetes Registry ⭐⭐⭐

Who can join:
Mothers diagnosed with gestational diabetes (currently pregnant or within 12 weeks postpartum)
Singleton pregnancy
Aged 18–50
Not currently taking steroids
No uncontrolled thyroid disease
No diagnosis of diabetes outside of pregnancy
Not currently participating in other weight-loss or lifestyle intervention studies
Not taking blood sugar-lowering or weight-control medications outside of pregnancy

Background

Mothers who have had gestational diabetes:
Are up to
7 times more likely
to develop type 2 diabetes in the future
Have a higher risk of
high blood pressure, fatty liver, and other cardiovascular diseases
Their children are more likely to develop
diabetes, overweight/obesity, or high blood pressure
by age 7

Problem

There is currently
no standardized guideline in Hong Kong
for postpartum follow-up of women with gestational diabetes.
Although these women are at higher risk for metabolic issues like hypertension, abnormal blood lipids, and obesity,
routine monitoring after pregnancy is lacking
.

Study Details (Free of Charge)

Participants will receive
4 health checkups over 3 years
:
1st checkup
: 6–12 weeks postpartum
2nd checkup
: 1 year later
3rd checkup
: 2 years later
4th checkup
: 3 years later
Location: CUHK Medical Centre

Annual Follow-Up Includes

Oral Glucose Tolerance Test
Blood tests (glucose, lipids, liver and kidney function)
Fibroscan
Skin AGE test (to examine cardiovascular risk)
Blood pressure, heart rate, and anthropometric measurements (height, weight, waist/hip circumference, InBody)
Questionnaire (health status, family history, diet and exercise habits, breastfeeding, etc.)
In the third year, children will be invited for skinfold thickness measurement and oral swab collection
Free digital platform to receive health information
Additionally,
high-risk participants
may be invited to join a
3-year diabetes prevention program
, including:
One-on-one guidance from registered dietitian and exercise instructor
A fitness tracker watch and continuous glucose monitors

Interested? Sign up via:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_es7l8ryzLKFuXie
Scan the QR code
WhatsApp: +852 6743 9107
For inquiries, feel free to WhatsApp +852 6743 9107.
Thank you again for your interest in this study
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

You are cordially invited to join our upcoming webinar - 【Recycling Fund - Info Session】on 17 Nov, 2026 (Tue) 11:00am - 12:00pm through ZOOM.
In this session, we are honoured to have Mr Sam Lee, Head of the Recycling Fund Secretariat under Hong Kong Productivity Council (HKPC), as our guest speaker. He will introduce the Recycling Fund Funding Scheme and provide details about the Enterprise Support Programme (ESP), with a special focus on Projects from New and Start-up Enterprises (SUP).
The ESP in the Recycling Fund offers matching funds to enhance recycling projects for enterprises. The maximum funding is HK$15 million for 10 projects per enterprise. Start-ups established within 5 years can apply for the SUP scheme, supporting innovative recycling ideas. The funding cap for SUP projects has increased from $0.5 million to $2 million per project to support diverse innovations.

title: CALL FOR PROPOSALS | Participation in the 17th Chinese National Arctic Research Expedition 2027 | HKPSIC
bodyText:

CALL FOR PROPOSALS | Participation in the 17th Chinese National Arctic Research Expedition 2027 | HKPSIC  - Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre
From: Yolanda Yim
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yolandayim@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

CALL FOR PROPOSALS
|
Participation in
the 17th
Chinese National Arctic
Research Expedition 2027
|
HKPSIC
An Opportunity to Conduct Research in A
rctic Regions
_______________________________________________________________________________
The Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC) is pleased to invite proposals from scientists and researchers interested in participating in the
17th
Chinese National Arctic
Research Expedition 2027
.
Research opportunities are available at
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2, Yellow River Station
and
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
in Arctic Regions. All proposals and personnel nominations will be reviewed and selected by the Polar Research Institute of China (PRIC).
This opportunity is primarily open to researchers from universities in Hong Kong.
Expedition Purpose
The expedition will be conducted for
scientific research purposes
.
Research Opportunities
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2
Quota:
Tentatively 1-2 participants
(Subject to adjustment based on the approved research proposals.)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 months at the station
Tentative departure from Shanghai aboard the icebreaker
Xuelong
or
Xuelong 2
in June or July 2027
Return to Shanghai in Sep or Oct 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Shanghai
Yellow River Station
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Longyearbyen to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Longyearbyen and from Hong Kong
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Akureyri and drive to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights from Hong Kong to Reykjavík, onward travel to Akureyri, and ground transportation to the station.
Priority consideration:
Applicants with existing research collaborations or academic connections in Iceland
Research Instruments
As the icebreakers
Xuelong
and
Xuelong 2
will depart from Shanghai, PRIC recommends that any required research instruments be shipped to Shanghai no later than
April-May
for loading and transportation to the Arctic research stations.
Health and Visa Requirements
Selected participants will be required to:
Complete a medical examination specified by PRIC
Submit a medical report for review
Obtain a Schengen visa for Yellow River Station or CIAO
Participants should allow sufficient time for medical examinations and visa applications.
Clothing and Equipment
PRIC will provide basic expedition clothing and equipment, including:
Expedition jackets
Trousers
Thermal wear
Sunglasses
Other essential gear
These items will be provided to selected participants before departure.
Expenses to Be Covered by Participants
Participants are responsible for all associated expenses, including:
International airfares
Accommodation on the stations before and after station entry/exit or during the expedition in the stations
(Accommodation on Xuelong or Xuelong 2 is provided free of charge)
Travel insurance
Visa application fees (if applicable)
Medical examination fees
Shipment and transportation costs for research instruments and equipment
Any other incidental expenses
Proposal Submission
Researchers who are able to meet the above requirements and schedule are invited to submit an email request to obtain the proposal template.
Submission Deadline
10 November 2026 (Tuesday)
All proposals will be forwarded to PRIC for evaluation and selection. HKPSIC will provide support to participating researchers and facilitate communications with PRIC throughout the application and preparation process.
Enquiries
Secretariat
Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC)
Email: hkpsic@cuhk.edu.hk
Tel: 3943 0345
We sincerely encourage interested researchers to take advantage of this unique opportunity to conduct scientific research in Arctic Regions and contribute to polar research collaboration.
We look forward to receiving your proposals.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Muse Moments | “Museum, Music & Wellbeing” Muse Moments｜「Museum, Music＆Wellbeing」 - Art Museum, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
From: Mark Choi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
artmuseum@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#Muse Moments “Museum, Music & Wellbeing”
A little music, a great moment
Music and the museum bring their different professional worlds together. On 20 November, the Art Museum’s Muse Moments will collaborate with two special guests - renowned musician Barry Chung whose work spans pop songs, film scores, and music for wellbeing; and Dr. Kai Tai Chan who is a psychiatrist, lyricist and writer.
Join Barry and Dr. Chan to experience a relaxed hour of music and conversation about wellbeing, moving freely between performance, immersion and sharing.
Date: 20 November 2026 (Friday)
Time: 17:30 – 18:30
Venue: Lee Hysan Atrium, Lo Kwee Seong Pavilion, Art Museum
Language: Cantonese
Co-organisers: CUHK Art Museum and CUHK Centre for Bioethics
#MuseMoments 「Museum, Music & Wellbeing」
關於音樂，也關於生活
音樂，是兩人不同專業背景下在文物館的交集。11月20日，文物館的 Muse Moments 將與兩位特別嘉賓合作，帶來不一樣的音樂體驗——著名音樂人鍾慶鴻 Barry Chung 的創作涵蓋流行曲、電影配樂及身心靈音樂；陳啓泰醫生既是精神科專科醫生，也是填詞人與作家。
兩位嘉賓將透過流動的演奏與分享，談談音樂，談談身心，與大家共度輕鬆一小時。
日期：2026年11月20日（星期五）
時間：17:30 – 18:30
地點：香港中文大學文物館羅桂祥閣利希慎廊
語言：粵語
合辦：香港中文大學文物館 及 香港中文大學生命倫理學中心
Registration and Details 報名及查看詳情 :
Click here 按此
The successful registrants can enjoy 50% off selected drinks at Ideaology, CUHK Art Museum, on 20 November. This offer is valid only on the day of the event.
成功登記活動的參加者，可於11月20日親臨 Ideaology 文物館店，以半價購買指定飲品。優惠僅限活動當日使用。
About Barry Chung
Barry is a veteran musician from Hong Kong. Having been working for almost 40 years in the music business, he is one of the most sought-after guitarists, producers and general musicians around. His well-known compositions include "信心花舍"(Eason Chan),"燕尾蝶"(Shine) and "勇"(Miriam Yeung). Barry has performed with numerous artistes and among them is Olivia Newton John where he acted as her backup singer. Barry has also won international music recognitions including the USA Song Writing Competition and Great American Song Contest.
Barry has long been fascinated by the healing and wellness music and in 2023 he has successfully completed a sound project ” The Rainbow-Chakras Nexus”, which is based on the 7 main Chakras in the human body, the 7 main colours of the rainbow and the 7 notes within the major scale in music. This sound project has won the silver medal for “Best New Age Album“ and “Best Producer’ awards from the 2025 Global Music Award and the “Best New Age Album” finalist in 2025 World Entertainment Awards.
About Kai Tai Chan
Dr. Kai Tai Chan is a specialist in psychiatry, lyricist, and writer. He currently serves in various interdisciplinary positions, including Clinical Professional Consultant and Associate Professor in Practice of Psychiatry (By Courtesy) in CU Medicine. Throughout the years, apart from clinical practice, he has been involved in various educational activities, service development as well as research activities. In addition to mental health and anti-stigmatization education and campaigns, recently, he has been advocating the development of Youth Mental Health in Hong Kong across different platforms.
To promote well-being in the community, he has been exploring the interplay of culture and mental health as well as advocating the use of music in promoting well-being. Following his previous book called 《多謝廣東歌 讓我好好過》, recently he collaborated with Professor Stephen Chu to co-author the recent book 《好在廣東歌》, further exploring the relationship of Cantopop and well-being and sharing the experiences of application of Cantopop in community well-being projects.
關於鍾慶鴻
Barry Chung 鍾慶鴻，香港樂壇一個為人熟悉的名字，曾創作多首獲獎流行金曲及廣告歌，並為眾多歌手擔任監製、編曲、結他手、和音等，包括Shine的《燕尾蝶》、陳奕迅的《信心花舍》以及楊千嬅的《勇》的作曲等。憑著他的音樂天賦及多年創作經驗，2006 年首次參與美國 USA Song Writing Competition ，憑“Once You Know”一曲奪得是次比賽之冠軍（純音樂組），成為首位奪得此項殊榮之中國人。而“Thirty Something”一曲亦為他帶來 Great American Song Contest 之榮譽大獎，足見他的音樂才華獲得國際音樂人的認同和肯定。
除了流行音樂，Barry 亦對身心靈音樂有着濃厚興趣。在 2023 年 Barry 成功地完成一個以七個主要脈輪及其顏色做主題的聲音專輯。這專輯亦囊括了 2025 年美國 Global Music Awards 的最佳新世代專輯以及最佳新世代專輯最佳監製獎的銀獎，以及 2025 年美國 World Entertainment Awards的最佳新世代專輯最後三強。
關於陳啓泰
陳啓泰醫生為精神科專科醫生、作詞人及作家，現身兼多項跨領域職務，當中包括中文大學醫學院臨床專業顧問及精神科專業應用副教授（禮任）。多年來，除了臨床工作外，他一直積極參與各類教學活動、服務發展及研究工作。除精神健康及反污名化教育與倡議外，近年他更透過不同平台積極推動香港青少年精神健康的發展。
為促進社會的幸福感，他持續探索文化與精神健康的相互作用，並倡導以音樂提升幸福感。繼舊作《多謝廣東歌 讓我好好過》，他與朱耀偉教授最近推出了《好在廣東歌》一書，進一步探討廣東歌與精神健康及幸福感的關係，以及初步社區應用的經驗。

A little music, a great moment
Music and the museum bring their different professional worlds together. On 20 November, the Art Museum’s Muse Moments will collaborate with two special guests - renowned musician Barry Chung whose work spans pop songs, film scores, and music for wellbeing; and Dr. Kai Tai Chan who is a psychiatrist, lyricist and writer.
Join Barry and Dr. Chan to experience a relaxed hour of music and conversation about wellbeing, moving freely between performance, immersion and sharing.

Time: 17:30 – 18:30
Venue: Lee Hysan Atrium, Lo Kwee Seong Pavilion, Art Museum
Language: Cantonese
Co-organisers: CUHK Art Museum and CUHK Centre for Bioethics

From: Queenie Chow
