We all know group projects can be... challenging. What if you had an
AI project manager
that breaks down tasks, writes meeting notes, and helps resolve disagreements?
Use Copilot
to keep your team on track and your project drama-free.
Prompt 1 — copy & paste it!
Break it down
"Our group project is: [describe]. We have 4 members and 3 weeks. Break into specific tasks with: 1) Clear deliverables per person 2) Dependencies 3) Deadlines 4) A risk and mitigation plan."
Prompt 2 — keep the conversation going!
Meeting minutes in seconds
"Here are rough notes from our group meeting: [paste notes]. Turn these into professional minutes with: attendees, key decisions, action items (who/what/when), and next meeting items."
Prompt 3 — go advanced!
Resolve disagreements
"Our team disagrees on [issue]. Person A thinks [A] and Person B thinks [B]. Give an objective pros/cons analysis, then suggest a compromise taking the best of both."
Why this works:
Copilot is the neutral third party every group project needs. No sides, no drama, just clear action plans!

Bonus tip:
Before final submission:
"Review our project for consistency in writing style, formatting, and tone — make it sound like one person wrote it"

for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

title: Simply Pocket Oasis Workshop 「靜系」掌心水苔球工作坊
bodyText:

Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
Simply Pocket Oasis Workshop 「靜系」掌心水苔球工作坊 - Shaw College
From: Jessie LI
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jessieli@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Every day, you're busy creating PowerPoint slides, essays, reports and CVs...
But when was the last time you created a moment of inner peace for yourself?
Join us to design and craft your own miniature Zen garden, and give yourself a moment to simply be. Through your five senses, reconnect with yourself and the present moment, while letting your body and mind truly rest.
Come and create your pocket oasis!
Date: 31 October 2026 (Sat)
Time: 10:00 - 12:00
Venue: LG501, Wen Lan Tang, Shaw College, CUHK
Quota: 24
Target: CUHK Students, Staff, Alumni and the General Public (Priorities are given to Friends of the Arts members and CUHK Undergraduate Students)
Fee: Please refer to the application form
Online Application:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13742389
Application Deadline: 16 October 2026 (Fri)
Enquiry: Ms. Chow (
florachow@cuhk.edu.hk/
3943 1549)
我們每天都在創造很多東西——PowerPoint、Essay、報告、CV…
卻很少創造一刻真正屬於自己的平靜。
這一次，用雙手打造一個掌心盆景，留下一段與自己同行的時間。
透過五感覺察，與自己和當下連結，
一邊設計並製作屬於你的掌心盆景，一邊讓身心好好休息。
快來打造你專屬的「掌心心靈綠洲」吧！
日期: 2026年10月31日 (星期六)
時間: 10:00 - 12:00
地點: 香港中文大學逸夫書院文瀾堂LG501
名額: 24人
對象: 中大學生、教職員、校友及公眾人士 (Friends of the Arts 會員及中大本科生優先)
費用: 請參考報名表
網上報名︰

florachow@cuhk.edu.hk

Gerald Choa Neuroscience Institute (GCNI) is now looking for student helpers for GCNI Symposium 30 November & 1 December 2026. Details are listed below:
Date:
30 November & 1 December 2026 (Monday & Tuesday)
Time:
8:15 am - 5:30 pm (Day 1), 9:15 - 1:00 (Day 2)
Venue:
YIA LT2
Duties:
Counter reception, poster design, IT support, logistics coordination, taking photos etc.
Hourly rate:
HK$64/hour
(Free lunch and refreshments will be provided)
Application link and deadline:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13743990
On or before 23 October 2026
Remarks:
A paid 2-hour briefing session will be held on 29 November 2026 (Sunday).
Only full time CUHK students are eligible to apply.
You must register for Student Helper Engagement Scheme before the event if appointed.
Non-local students must present your “No Objection Letter” issued by the Immigration Department.
Preference will be given to applicants available for the briefing session on 29 Nov, the whole session on 30 Nov (08:15 - 17:30) and the whole session on 1 Dec (09:15 - 13:00).
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and receive our confirmation email after the application deadline.

bodyText:

From: Dorothy Yuen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cuoaa@cuhk.edu.hk

禪繞 X 瑪雅印記初探
找回真正的自己快樂做自己
瑪雅印記是什麼？中美洲古瑪雅文明的智慧，說著每個人出生時都有與生俱來的『天賦才華』。此課程將引領你找到『它』，用另一角度認識自己，運用在你的生活/人際關係//工作/家庭中。
「一筆一畫，無限可能。」禪繞是一場筆與紙的自我對話，發現更多未知的自己。不需任何繪畫技巧，沒有對與錯，沒有美與醜，只需筆隨心轉，一筆一畫，療癒心靈，放鬆地繪出自己的世界。
禪繞畫是一種簡單而自由的繪畫技巧，易於入門，可以幫助人們學會專注和集中注意力，並激發創造力和想像力。這些因素都使得禪繞畫成為一種非常適合作為藝術入門的繪畫技巧。
它們都是友善的工具，讓你們禪繞遇見<我的瑪雅, 我的天賦>。

bodyText:

Announcements
Mindfulness Workshop: Connect Your Body, Mind & Nature Certificate Upon Completion of All Four Sessions 【正念工作坊】連結身心與自然｜完成四節可獲出席證書 - Department of Educational Administration and Policy
From: WONG Hoi Yan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155219686@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

心身連結正念工作坊
本工作坊旨在協助參加者學習正念的態度與技巧，連結當下的身心狀態，增進對韌性（resilience）及自然為本療癒概念的理解，並透過五感體驗與大自然建立更深的連結。

日期及時間
• 正念基礎：2026年11月3日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
• 覺察情緒：2026年11月10日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
• 智慧的心：2026年11月17日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
• 連結世界：2026年11月24日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.

地點
香港中文大學校園（崇基校園），活動將於戶外及室內場地進行。

語言
以廣東話為主，英語輔助。

重要事項
• 每位學生嚮導最少須參加兩節正念體驗工作坊。 • 首兩節工作坊為必須出席，參加者必須出席：
2026年11月3日：正念基礎
2026年11月10日：覺察情緒
能夠出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲優先考慮。
出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲發出席證書 
由於部分活動將於戶外進行，參加者請穿著舒適、適合戶外活動的衣物及鞋履
本活動由香港中文大學教育學院 PDTL Grant 贊助。

計畫負責人及導師
劉雅詩博士
註冊中學教師
香港中文大學教育行政與政策學系高級講師
自2007年起致力向職前教師及在職教師推廣靜觀（正念）。

查詢
李小姐：
chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
成功報名的參加者將獲電郵通知。
報名連結：
https://forms.gle/YLKv4soaARwBHkgF8

Mindfulness & Body-Mind Connection Workshop
This workshop aims to help participants cultivate mindfulness attitudes and skills, develop a deeper connection with the present moment and their body-mind experience, and enhance their understanding of resilience and nature-based healing. Through experiential activities involving the five senses, participants will also have the opportunity to build a closer connection with nature.

Dates and Times
• Mindfulness Foundations: 3 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. (Mandatory) • Cultivating Emotional Awareness: 10 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. (Mandatory) • The Wisdom of the Heart: 17 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. • Connecting with the World: 24 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.

Venue
The Chinese University of Hong Kong campus, Chung Chi Campus. The workshop will take place in a combination of outdoor and indoor settings.

Language
Primarily Cantonese, with English support.

Important Notes
• Each student guide is required to attend at least two mindfulness experiential workshop sessions. • The first two sessions are mandatory. Participants must attend:
3 November 2026: Mindfulness Foundations
10 November 2026: Cultivating Emotional Awareness
• Priority will be given to students who are able to attend all four sessions.
• Students who attend all four workshop sessions will receive an attendance certificate 
• As some activities will be conducted outdoors, participants are advised to wear comfortable clothing and suitable footwear for outdoor activities 
This activity is sponsored by the PDTL Grant of the Faculty of Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Course Trainer
Dr. Lau Ngar Sze
Registered Secondary School Teacher
Senior Lecturer, Department of Educational Administration and Policy,
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Dr. Lau has been promoting mindfulness among pre-service and in-service teachers since 2007.

Enquiries
Miss Fiona Li:
chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk
Successful applicants will be notified by email.
Registration link

本工作坊旨在協助參加者學習正念的態度與技巧，連結當下的身心狀態，增進對韌性（resilience）及自然為本療癒概念的理解，並透過五感體驗與大自然建立更深的連結。

日期及時間
• 正念基礎：2026年11月3日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
• 覺察情緒：2026年11月10日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.（必須出席）
• 智慧的心：2026年11月17日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.
• 連結世界：2026年11月24日（星期二）12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.

地點
香港中文大學校園（崇基校園），活動將於戶外及室內場地進行。

語言
以廣東話為主，英語輔助。

重要事項
• 每位學生嚮導最少須參加兩節正念體驗工作坊。 • 首兩節工作坊為必須出席，參加者必須出席：
2026年11月3日：正念基礎
2026年11月10日：覺察情緒
能夠出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲優先考慮。
出席全部四節工作坊的同學將獲發出席證書 
由於部分活動將於戶外進行，參加者請穿著舒適、適合戶外活動的衣物及鞋履
本活動由香港中文大學教育學院 PDTL Grant 贊助。

計畫負責人及導師
劉雅詩博士
註冊中學教師
香港中文大學教育行政與政策學系高級講師
自2007年起致力向職前教師及在職教師推廣靜觀（正念）。

chingtungli@cuhk.edu.hk

https://forms.gle/YLKv4soaARwBHkgF8

Mindfulness & Body-Mind Connection Workshop
This workshop aims to help participants cultivate mindfulness attitudes and skills, develop a deeper connection with the present moment and their body-mind experience, and enhance their understanding of resilience and nature-based healing. Through experiential activities involving the five senses, participants will also have the opportunity to build a closer connection with nature.

Dates and Times
• Mindfulness Foundations: 3 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. (Mandatory) • Cultivating Emotional Awareness: 10 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. (Mandatory) • The Wisdom of the Heart: 17 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. • Connecting with the World: 24 November 2026 (Tuesday), 12:30 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.

Venue
The Chinese University of Hong Kong campus, Chung Chi Campus. The workshop will take place in a combination of outdoor and indoor settings.

Language
Primarily Cantonese, with English support.

Important Notes
• Each student guide is required to attend at least two mindfulness experiential workshop sessions. • The first two sessions are mandatory. Participants must attend:
3 November 2026: Mindfulness Foundations
10 November 2026: Cultivating Emotional Awareness
• Priority will be given to students who are able to attend all four sessions.
• Students who attend all four workshop sessions will receive an attendance certificate 
• As some activities will be conducted outdoors, participants are advised to wear comfortable clothing and suitable footwear for outdoor activities 
This activity is sponsored by the PDTL Grant of the Faculty of Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Course Trainer
Dr. Lau Ngar Sze
Registered Secondary School Teacher
Senior Lecturer, Department of Educational Administration and Policy,
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Dr. Lau has been promoting mindfulness among pre-service and in-service teachers since 2007.

社區藥房提供的服務

藥劑師如何成為您可靠的社區健康夥伴

Sharing by HIA Community Pharmacy: Understanding Community Pharmacy Services

Free Health Check for Chronic Disease
Have you ever wondered how pharmacists can support your health beyond dispensing medicines?
Join us for an informative sharing session by a pharmacist from
Health In Action (HIA) Community Pharmacy
and learn how community pharmacy services can support you and your family in maintaining good health.

Date:
16 October 2026 (Friday)

Time:
2 p.m. - 3 p.m.

Venue:
Activity Room 1–3, Quarryside, 20 Hoi Shin Lane, Quarry Bay

Language:
English

Speaker:
Pharmacist from Health In Action Community Pharmacy

Quota:
20 participants
⭐⭐⭐
Free health check for blood pressure, blood glucose and cholesterol will be available after the talk!!
‼⭐
What will you learn?
The role of pharmacists in primary healthcare
Services provided by community pharmacies
Safe use of medications and medication management
Support available for minor ailments and chronic disease management
How pharmacists can become your trusted community health partners
Health In Action believes that community pharmacies can serve as an important first point of contact for healthcare services. Through health education, medication management, and community-based pharmacy services, pharmacists play an important role in helping individuals and families stay healthy and informed.
This session is suitable for members of multicultural communities, community workers, caregivers, and anyone interested in learning more about healthcare services in Hong Kong.

Register here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3QnJthMMwdTKD2K
Places are limited and will be allocated on a
first-come, first-served basis
. Successful registrants will receive a WhatsApp confirmation message.

Successfully registered participants who attend the event will receive a special souvenir!
‼⭐
We look forward to seeing you and exploring how pharmacists can support healthier communities together!
JCSATH

齊來認識腸道健康 Trust Your Gut: From Early Life to Everyday Wellbeing 免費健康篩查驗三高   - The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: The Jockey Club S.A.T.H. Project for Healthy Families (JCSATH)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jcsath@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

TRUST YOUR GUT
齊來認識腸道健康
免費健康篩查驗三高
您知道嗎？腸道的功能不僅僅是消化食物！腸道微生物群（Gut Microbiome）對我們的身體健康、心理健康、免疫力、睡眠質素以及整體生活質素都擔當著重要角色。研究顯示，我們的飲食習慣、睡眠質素、運動量，甚至壓力水平，都會影響腸道健康。
誠邀您參加這個內容豐富且實用的健康講座，一同了解如何透過簡單的生活習慣，促進腸道健康，提升整體身心健康。
認識什麼是腸道微生物群，以及它如何在生命早期建立
了解腸道健康、免疫系統及心理健康之間的關係
認識微生物群研究的方法，以及您如何參與相關研究
了解睡眠、運動、飲食及壓力如何影響腸道健康
獲取維持健康生活方式的實用貼士
無論您希望改善個人健康、關注家人的身心健康，還是單純對腸道健康感興趣，都歡迎參加！

日期：
2026年10月16日（星期五）
⏰
時間：
中午12:00 至 下午1:00

地點：
鰂魚涌海濱活動空間 Quarryside 活動室 1 至 3（鰂魚涌海善里 20 號）

名額：
20人

語言：
英語（設有廣東話及南亞語言傳譯服務）
⭐⭐⭐完成健康講座後設有免費健康篩查, 量度血壓、血糖、膽固醇
!
‼⭐

歡迎家長攜同子女一同參加。

報名連結
：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eIZxGg6CKyBC9ts

查詢
：
JCSATH WhatsApp 6104 9535
一齊了解日常生活中的小習慣，如何為腸道健康帶來大改變，提升整體身心健康！
成功登記及出席將獲贈精美紀念品乙份‼⭐
Trust Your Gut: Health Talk Free Health Check for Chronic Disease
Did you know that your gut does much more than digest food? The gut microbiome plays an important role in our physical health, mental wellbeing, immunity, sleep, and overall quality of life. Research shows that what we eat, how we sleep, how active we are, and even our stress levels can influence our gut health.
Join us for an informative and practical health talk to learn how simple lifestyle choices can support a healthier gut and improve overall wellbeing.
Learn what the gut microbiome is and how it is established in early life

title: 超越現實的畫作：藝術 × 混合實境（Mixed Reality）體驗
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Announcements
超越現實的畫作：藝術 × 混合實境（Mixed Reality）體驗   - The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: The Jockey Club S.A.T.H. Project for Healthy Families (JCSATH)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jcsath@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

超越現實的畫作：藝術
×
混合實境（
Mixed Reality
）體驗

誠邀你參加一個結合藝術同混合實境（MR）科技嘅創意工作坊，與來自不同文化背景的朋友一同創作一幅屬於大家的立體藝術作品，共同描繪香港故事。
參加者將透過 MR 技術在同一個實體及虛擬空間進行 3D 繪畫，分享自己對香港的回憶、感受、生活點滴和想法。你可以自由創作、與其他參加者合作，或者在之前參加者的作品上加入新元素。隨著創作慢慢累積，一幅集合不同文化背景、不同生活經歷的大型立體藝術作品將會逐步形成。
體驗嶄新混合實境（MR）科技
在沉浸式空間進行 3D 創作
用藝術分享你眼中的香港
與不同文化背景的參加者互動交流
無需任何藝術或科技經驗
歡迎所有文化背景人士參加。
即使你不想親身創作，都歡迎以觀賞者身份參與，透過觀賞專用頭戴裝置欣賞創作過程，以及不斷演變的立體藝術作品。

日期：
2026年10月15日（星期四）
⏰
時間：
下午2:00 至 5:30

地點：
鰂魚涌海濱活動空間 Quarryside  舍區 活動室 1 至 3（鰂魚涌海善里 20 號）

名額：
20位參加者

語言
:
英語為主 (現場設有廣東話及南亞語言翻譯)
一齊探索藝術和科技如何促進跨文化交流，透過創作認識彼此，從不同角度重新欣賞香港！

報名連結：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0TGkqUSP8Dc5WqW

報名截止日期：
2026年10月11日（星期日）

查詢：
JCSATH WhatsApp 6104 9535
注意事項
• 名額有限，先到先得。
• 成功報名者將於活動最少2日前收到 WhatsApp 確認通知。如未收到確認訊息，則表示未能成功獲得名額。
無需
任何繪畫技巧或科技知識，只要帶住你的好奇心、創意，和屬於你的香港故事一同參與！

=====================================================================

Drawing Beyond Reality: Art & MR Experience

What does Hong Kong look like through your eyes?
Join us for a unique
Mixed Reality (MR) art workshop
where people from different cultural backgrounds come together to create a shared
3D artwork
about life in Hong Kong.
Using
MR technology
, participants will draw and create in the
same physical and virtual space
, expressing their memories, experiences, feelings, and perspectives of Hong Kong. You may create your own artwork, collaborate with others, or add to drawings created by previous participants. Together, we will build a collective 3D artwork that reflects the
diverse stories
and voices of our community.
Experience Mixed Reality technology
Create artwork in a 3D immersive space
Explore memories, experiences, hopes, and everyday life in Hong Kong
No art or technology experience required
Participate as a creator or observer
We welcome participants from all cultural backgrounds, including
members from multicultural communities
and Chinese communities.
Even if you do not wish to create artwork yourself, you can still join as an observer and explore the evolving virtual artwork through dedicated observation headsets.

Date:
15 October 2026 (Thursday)
⏰
Time:
2:00 PM - 5:30 PM

Venue:
Quarryside

Quota:
20 registered participants

Language:
English (interpretation available in Cantonese and South Asian languages)
Come and explore how art and technology can bring people together, spark conversations, and help us see Hong Kong through one another's eyes.
Register here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0TGkqUSP8Dc5WqW
Registration Deadline: 11 October 2026 (Sunday)
Enquiries: JCSATH WhatsApp 6104 9535
Notes
• Due to limited places, registration is on a first-come, first-served basis.
• Successful registrants will receive a WhatsApp confirmation at least 2 days before the event. If you do not receive a confirmation message, your registration is considered unsuccessful.
Open to people from all cultural backgrounds. Let's explore our stories, communities, and experiences together through creativity and technology.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Master of Social Science in Sustainable Tourism (MSSST) Programme, Department of Geography and Resource Management
The Department of Geography and Resource Management (GRM) at CUHK has long been at the forefront of sustainability education, research, and practice at local, regional, and global levels. Established in 2007, the MSSST Programme is a pioneering and distinctive postgraduate programme that advances sustainable tourism through interdisciplinary education, experiential learning, research-informed practice, and engagement with industry, government, and communities. Building on its strengths in sustainable tourism, resource management, tourism governance, and destination development, the Programme continues to evolve in response to emerging challenges and opportunities in Hong Kong, the Greater Bay Area, China, and beyond.
Join a vibrant learning community committed to creating positive change through tourism. Through innovative and experiential learning, the Programme develops responsible sustainable tourism leaders equipped with the knowledge, professional skills, and ethical values to contribute to industry innovation, community wellbeing, and a more sustainable, inclusive, and resilient future.
You are welcomed to register via the link above. Should you have any questions, please feel free to email us at MSSST@cuhk.edu.hk.

Format: Zoom

Master of Science in GeoInformation Science and Smart Cities
This programme is designed for graduates from a range of disciplines, specifically for graduates who have completed an undergraduate degree in geography, ecology, environmental science, surveying, civil engineering, urban planning, GIS or remote sensing, or practitioners or officers/officials in the similar fields who seek to develop a career or improve their careers in relation to applied GIS/remote sensing technologies. This programme aims at providing students with a solid conceptual framework and technical know-how by enhancing their skills and equipping them with hands-on experience. It also introduces the state-of-the-art geo-spatial information technologies and provides students with the capability to manage and apply the latest technologies to solve real life problems. In recent years, the trend of smart cities development (i.e., urban areas that use different types of electronic methods and sensors to collect data in improving the operations across the city) has been getting apparently important, while geoinformation science is the major tool for materializing the concept of smart cities.

Announcements
Recruitment of Student Internship 招募實習學生 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Edwin Chung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
shunkitchung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院研究團隊現正進行一項
社區研究。本計劃透過免費提供空氣清新機，幫助居住在空氣質素欠佳環境
的 6 至 17 歲哮喘兒童及青少年改善居住環境。
我們誠邀中大本科生加入參與實習，
一同走進社區，透過科學方法協助家庭。
工作範疇
- 研究期間：即日起至 2027 年 10 月 31 日（按團隊編排彈性參與）
- 協助研究團隊在指定的日期和地點進行研究對象招募。
- 按日子到研究對象的住所設置空氣監測儀器、放置空氣清新機，並為研究對象進行呼吸測試。
- 執行研究團隊指派的其他工作。
招募條件
- 現正就讀大學學士學位課程的學生（醫學、護理、公共衛生或相關課
程更佳）。
- 具備良好溝通技巧，能操流利廣東話（具適量普通話水平更佳）。
- 熟悉基本電腦應用。
報名方式
如有興趣參與本研究實習，請將個人履歷傳送至電郵：jchomes@cuhk.edu.hk
（郵件標題請註明：申請哮喘兒童研究學生實習)
聯絡及查詢
香港中文大學賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院
負責同事: Sang/Edwin
電話：(852) 2252 8744
電郵：jchomes@cuhk.edu.hk
The research team from the Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)
is currently conducting a community study. This project aims to improve the living conditions of children and adolescents aged 6 to 17 with asthma who reside in poor air quality environments by providing them with free air purifiers.
We sincerely invite CUHK undergraduate students to join us as interns to step into the community and assist these families through scientific methods.
Scope of Work
Research Period:
From now until October 31, 2027 (flexible participation based on the team's schedule)
Participant Recruitment: Assist the research team in recruiting study subjects at designated dates and locations.
Home Visits & Testing: Visit the subjects' homes to set up air monitoring equipment, place air purifiers, and conduct respiratory tests for the subjects.
Other Duties:
Execute other tasks assigned by the research team.
Recruitment Criteria
Education:
Current undergraduate students pursuing a bachelor's degree (preferably in Medicine, Nursing, Public Health, or related programs).
Languages:
Good communication skills, fluent in Cantonese (proficiency in Mandarin is a plus).
Skills:
Familiar with basic computer applications.
Application Method
If you are interested in participating in this research internship, please send your resume to jchomes@cuhk.edu.hk
(Please use the subject line: Application for Pediatric Asthma Study Student Internship
).
Contact and Inquiries
Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK
Contact Persons:
Sang / Edwin
Phone:
(852) 2252 8744
Email:
jchomes@cuhk.edu.hk
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Subject: 研究資助局公眾講座 - 兒童發展、學習與家庭介入(Research Grants Council Public Lectures to be conducted in Cantonese)
香港高等院校進行了很多令人振奮的學術研究計劃。為了讓市民更了解本地研究的重要性及價值，研究資助局定期舉辦公眾講座，向大眾分享最新研究成果。
研資局將於今年﹙2026﹚舉辦一系列與STEAM教育相關的公眾講座，講題包括人工智能與文物保育、網上訂價、兒童教育及宇宙探索。這些講座旨在提升市民對相關方面最新研究成果的認識。講座詳細內容如下：講座以粵語進行。免費入場，座位先到先得，有興趣人士亦可於網上收看講座現場直播或稍後重温。詳細內容如下：(
https://www.ugc.edu.hk/big5/rgc/about/events/lectures/lectures.html
)
The Hong Kong higher education sector has undertaken many exciting academic research projects. To raise public awareness of the significance and values of the local research work, the Research Grants Council regularly organises public lectures to share the latest research results with the public.
This year (2026), the RGC has organised a series of public lectures related to STEAM education, covering topics including cultural preservation with artificial intelligence, online pricing, children education, and universe exploration (conducted in Cantonese). These lectures aim to enhance the awareness of the latest researches in related areas. Please refer to Chinese version for more details.

When their village is devastated and their family is forced to flee, siblings

bodyText:

[Webinar] Understanding Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) [網上講座]認識多內分泌代謝性卵巢綜合症 (多囊卵巢綜合症) - The Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology (O&G)
From: Cynthia Lai
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sukhanlai@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
今年5月，醫學界將多囊卵巢綜合症（Polycystic Ovary Syndrome, PCOS）重新命名為多內分泌代謝性卵巢綜合症(Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome, PMOS)，因為它不僅是婦科問題，還涉及內分泌和代謝失調。香港中文大學醫學院的研究更指出，PMOS 不僅影響患者本人，還可能增加下一代在心臟健康、代謝、生殖及糖尿病方面的風險，顯示此症對女性及家庭健康有深遠影響。
為了讓大眾更深入了解，本中心將舉行「認識多內分泌代謝性卵巢綜合症 (多囊卵巢綜合症)」網上講座，誠邀大眾參與，一同掌握最新資訊。講座詳情如下：
日期： 10 月 26 日 (星期一)
時間： 下午 5:30 – 6:30
平台： Zoom（廣東話進行）
費用：全免，歡迎所有人士參與
主持： 鍾佩樺醫生
講者： 馬青雲醫生、張麗冰醫生、吳逸晞博士
報名：立即掃描海報上的 QR code 或擊點
https://forms.gle/PGVPd42VcXTxHGc8A
查詢電話：3505 1456
Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) has been renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) this May, as medical experts have recognized that it is not only a gynecological condition but also involves endocrine and metabolic disorders. Research from The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)’s Faculty of Medicine (CU Medicine) further indicates that PMOS affects not only patients themselves but may also increase risks for the next generation in areas such as heart health, metabolism, reproduction, and diabetes—highlighting its profound impact on women’s and family health.
To help the public gain deeper understanding, our center will host an online seminar: “Understanding Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome)” We warmly invite everyone to join and stay informed with the latest updates.
Date: October 26 (Monday)
Time: 5:30 PM – 6:30 PM
Platform: Zoom (conducted in Cantonese)
Fee: Free of charge, open to all
Moderator: Doctor Chung Pui Wah Jacqueline
Speakers: Doctor Ma Ching Wan Ronald, Doctor Cheung Lai Ping, Dr. Ng Yat Hey Noel

From: Horatio Gong

The Department of Social Work is delighted to share that the Research Programme for Aging and Disabilities has invited
Prof. Nathan Boucher
, Associate Professor of Public Policy, Nursing, and Medicine at Duke University, to offer a research seminar on “Community Engagement as a Public Policy Imperative in Caregiving Research”. This seminar will be held in hybrid mode (in-person & Zoom).
We warmly invite you to attend the seminar. For details, please find in the attached poster and below:
Time: 4 November 2026 (Wednesday); 2:30 p.m.-4:00 p.m.
Speaker: Prof. Nathan Boucher, Associate Professor of Public Policy, Nursing, and Medicine at Duke University
Venue: Room 520, Chen Kou Bun Building, CUHK (
Google Maps
) & Zoom
Registration: Please register via
this link
or scan the QR code in the poster
About the Seminar: Community engagement is essential to relevant and equitable aging and caregiving research. Dr. Nathan Boucher argues that lived experience should be treated as a form of data and incorporated throughout the research lifecycle. Older adults, family caregivers, clinicians, community organizations, and system leaders can help identify meaningful outcomes, expose structural inequities, and reveal contextual factors that administrative and clinical datasets often miss. Partnership-driven approaches—including interviews, focus groups, advisory councils, listening sessions, and user-centered design—can improve construct validity, feasibility, implementation, and policy translation. Community engagement also reduces research waste by aligning questions and interventions with the priorities of those most affected. Examples from aging, Veterans’ health, homelessness, and the direct care workforce illustrate how engagement can refine research questions, identify unintended consequences, and generate more responsive practices and policies. The presentation concludes that investing in engagement infrastructure is not optional; it is fundamental to producing sustainable, legitimate, and meaningful health systems research.
About the Speaker: Nathan Boucher is an expert in assessing patient and caregiver experiences during serious illness. As a Research Scientist with US Veterans Administration Health Systems Research and Associate Professor at Duke University, he specializes in both qualitative and intervention research at the intersection of social care and healthcare for older populations in need. Dr. Boucher leads projects to support family caregivers and older adults—including those assisting older adults re-entering the community from prison—and develops innovative interventions for families living with dementia and other serious illness. Dr. Boucher’s multidisciplinary perspective bridges clinical practice, health/social policy, and community engagement to drive meaningful advances in health and social supports for older adults.
Should you have any enquiries, please feel free to contact Mr. Horatio Gong at 39431709 or
horatiogong@cuhk.edu.hk
.
Thank you very much.

From: Horatio Gong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

The Department of Social Work is delighted to share that the Youth and Childhood Research Programme and the Family and Group Practice Research Programme has invited
Prof. Christopher Wretman
, Associate Professor/Senior Lecturer in Quantitative Research Methods at School of Social and Political Science, The University of Edinburgh, to offer a research seminar on “Current Approaches to Child Abuse Response in Scotland: The “Child’s House” Model”
We warmly invite you to attend the seminar. For details, please find the attached poster and below:
Time: 2:00pm-3:30pm, 16 October 2026 (Friday)
Speaker: Prof. Christopher Wretman, Associate Professor/Senior Lecturer in Quantitative Research Methods, School of Social and Political Science, The University of Edinburgh
Venue: Room 509, T. C. Cheng Building, CUHK (
Google Maps
)
Registration: Please register via
this link
or scan the QR code in the poster
About the Seminar: Since about 2021, Scotland has been implementing a series of interventions translated as “Child’s House” that seek to transform the coordination of service delivery in cases of child abuse. This work is driven by the following key question: "What happens to a child after they report/disclose abuse?" And, as a follow-up: “How can stakeholders make this process better for children and their families?" Realizing that traditional responses are often varied across police, health, education, and social work settings, and can feel traumatic and draining, “Child’s House” has been adapted in Scotland from a European model with a focus on co-located, multi-disciplinary, and inter-agency service delivery that hopes to simplify and improve child abuse response. “Child’s House” offers a shared spaced where different service provides can work together to deliver services to address children's rights to safety, justice, and recovery. An experienced team at the University of Edinburgh is leading efforts to promote and evaluate “Child’s House” in Scotland with a vision for changing how children experience services after abuse.
This lecture will cover four points. First, a discussion of current child abuse response legislation and policy frameworks in Scotland. Second, an overview of the “Child’s House” intervention model. Third, an overview of the University of Edinburgh team’s ongoing evaluation approaches. Fourth, and finally, preliminary findings and implications for global approaches to child protection.
Should you have any enquiries, please feel free to contact Mr. Horatio Gong at 3943 1709 or
horatiogong@cuhk.edu.hk
.
Thank you very much.

https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx

- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html

協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/EN/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/TC/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/SC/index.aspx

title: (Un)Seen | Our Moments with Loneliness 今日一起為孤獨留步 (20 – 30 Oct 2026)
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Events / Activities
(Un)Seen | Our Moments with Loneliness 今日一起為孤獨留步 (20 – 30 Oct 2026)  - WACC, OSA
From: Wellness and Counselling Centre, Office of Student Affairs
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
waccactivities@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
(Please scroll down for the Traditional Chinese version.)
(Un)Seen | Our Moments with Loneliness
Presented by the Wellness and Counselling Centre, Office of Student Affairs
Loneliness often goes unnoticed, quietly woven into our daily lives. Through stories, art, and immersive experiences, we warmly invite you to reflect on these unseen emotions and transform them into connections.
Take a moment to slow down, see others, and be seen.
⭐
Exhibition
Through student artworks, personal reflections, psychoeducational content, multimedia, and interactive installations, the exhibition explores the many dimensions of loneliness in university life. By sharing students’ voices and experiences, it seeks to foster greater connection, compassion, and understanding within the University community.
Date:
20 – 30/10/2026
Opening Hours:
Monday to Friday | 10:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.
Saturday | 10:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.
Closed on Sunday
Venue:
G/F & i-LOUNGE, 3/F, Yasumoto International Academic Park
All CUHK members are welcome.
⭐
Workshop and Talk Series
Explore the complexities of loneliness and discover practical coping strategies through over 15 talks, workshops and interactive drop-in activities under the themes "Shape of Loneliness" and "Dance with Loneliness". Join us in reflecting on different experiences of loneliness while learning ways to foster connection and well-being. Quota is limited, and pre-registration is needed.
Click
here
for workshop details and registration.
⭐
Instagram Photo Challenge
What does loneliness look like through your lens? Join our Instagram Photo Challenge and capture a moment, place, or scene on campus that reflects the theme of loneliness—you might just discover new meanings and something unexpected!
Participating students will have the chance to win exciting prizes, including Kodak Charmera Blind Box Camera, Fujifilm Instax Mini instant cameras, and more!
Follow
sunshineatcuhk_osa_wacc
on Instagram for challenge details and participation details.
Stay connected with us:
Instagram:
sunshineatcuhk_osa_wacc
Website:
https://wacc.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/unseen-our-moments-with-loneliness/
Enquiry: waccactivities@cuhk.edu.hk / 3943 7208
*************************************************
「(Un)Seen | 今日一起為孤獨留步」
學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心呈獻
孤獨常常不被察覺，但卻又悄悄地隱藏在我們的日常之中。透過故事、藝術作品、沉浸式體驗及工作坊等，我們誠邀你一同探索這些未被看見的情緒，並將它們轉化為彼此的連結。
不妨放慢腳步，給自己一些時間及空間——看見他人，也讓自己被看見
。
⭐
展覽
透過學生藝術創作、個人反思、心理健康教育資訊、多媒體展示及互動裝置，展覽帶領參觀著探討大學生活中孤獨的多重面向。藉由分享同學們的聲音與經歷，促進中大社群成員之間的連結、同理心與彼此理解。
日期:
2026年10月20至30日
開放時間 :
星期一至五 | 上午10時至下午6時
星期六 | 上午10時至下午4時
星期日休館
地點 :
康本國際學術園 地下及3樓 i-LOUNGE
歡迎所有中大成員參觀。
⭐
工作坊及講座系列
以「孤獨的形狀」及「與孤獨共舞」為主題，超過 15 場的講座、工作坊及互動活動帶領參加者認識孤獨、探索孤獨的複雜面向，學習實用的應對策略，並從中反思不同的孤獨經驗，建立更有意義的人際連結與身心健康。名額有限，須預先報名。
按
此處
查看活動詳情及報名。
⭐
Instagram大挑戰
在你的鏡頭下，孤獨是什麼模樣？
參加我們的Instagram挑戰吧! 在中大校園裡捕捉屬於你的「孤獨的形狀」、角落或畫面。透過你的獨特視角，也許會發現意想不到的驚喜。
參與同學有機會贏取豐富獎品，包括Kodak Charmera相機盲盒、Fujifilm Instax Mini即影即有相機等。
追蹤Instagram專頁 @
sunshineatcuhk_osa_wacc
，了解活動詳情及參加方法。
歡迎透過以下途徑了解更多：
Instagram:
sunshineatcuhk_osa_wacc
網站:
https://wacc.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/unseen-our-moments-with-loneliness/
查詢: waccactivities@cuhk.edu.hk / 3943 7208
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

ericacheng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We are recruiting volunteer native speakers of Hindi, Punjabi, Urdu, and/or Tamil to assist with recording a list of vocabulary items and short phrases. This project aims to
support children from ethnically diverse backgrounds
in learning Cantonese, English, and their home languages.
You must be:
1. Aged 18 or above;
2. A native speaker of Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, and/or Urdu;
3. Able to read Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, and/or Urdu;
4. Able to perform the recording task on the CUHK campus.
Non-CUHK volunteers are also welcome.
Details:
• Location: Academic Building No. 2, CUHK
• Duration: Approximately 1.5–2 hours
• Task: You will be asked to audio record a set of vocabulary items and short phrases in the language(s) you speak.
If you are interested, please fill in the form via the following link: https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741813
For any enquires, please contact Ms. Erica CHENG via email at ericacheng@cuhk.edu.hk

【
陸碳展覽回歸，拆解植被生態與碳循環 The Terrestrial Carbon Exhibition Returns: Unlocking Vegetated Ecosystems and the Carbon Cycle】
上次錯過左我地公眾展覽嘅朋友，我地返黎啦! 想了解陸地植被生態系統同碳循環嘅關係？咁就要黎參觀我哋嘅公眾展覽–「陸地植被生態系統在碳循環的關鍵角色」，我地會同大家拆解森林、灌木叢、草地點樣封存同儲存二氧化碳，仲會講解大嶼山植被嘅分佈狀況添～
Missed our last public exhibition? We are back! Want to discover the connection between terrestrial vegetated ecosystems and the carbon cycle? Come and join our public exhibition on the "Key Roles of Terrestrial Vegetated Ecosystems in Carbon Cycling". We will explain how forests, shrublands, and grasslands sequester and store CO2, and also provide an overview of the vegetation distribution in Lantau Island~
展覽日期 Exhibition Period：8-14 October 2026
展覽地點 Exhibition Venue：荃灣白田壩街45號南豐紗廠1樓M4 Atrium
M4 Atrium, 1/F, The Mills, 45 Pak Tin Par Street, Tsuen Wan
歡迎Share出去畀朋友都睇下，順手Like
同關注，一齊嚟認識陸地植被嘅重要性，為氣候行動加把勁！
Feel free to share it with friends, and don't forget to like
and follow. Let's understand the importance of terrestrial vegetation together and make efforts for climate action!

上次錯過左我地公眾展覽嘅朋友，我地返黎啦! 想了解陸地植被生態系統同碳循環嘅關係？咁就要黎參觀我哋嘅公眾展覽–「陸地植被生態系統在碳循環的關鍵角色」，我地會同大家拆解森林、灌木叢、草地點樣封存同儲存二氧化碳，仲會講解大嶼山植被嘅分佈狀況添～
Missed our last public exhibition? We are back! Want to discover the connection between terrestrial vegetated ecosystems and the carbon cycle? Come and join our public exhibition on the "Key Roles of Terrestrial Vegetated Ecosystems in Carbon Cycling". We will explain how forests, shrublands, and grasslands sequester and store CO2, and also provide an overview of the vegetation distribution in Lantau Island~

第一講
題目：孟子論人之所欲
主持：香港中文大學哲學系教授Prof. David Chai
日期：2026年10月21日（星期三）
時間：下午6時30分至下午8時
地點：香港中文大學邵逸夫堂
（本講座於書院雙週會內舉行）
第二講
題目：早期儒家倫理的共同基礎
主持：香港中文大學哲學系姚治華教授
日期：2026年10月22日（星期四）
時間：下午4時30分至下午6時15分
地點：香港中文大學行政樓地下祖堯堂
（本講座由香港中文大學新亞書院與哲學系合辦）
第三講
題目：死後生命在早期儒學中的相關性
主持：香港中文大學哲學系鄭澤綿教授
日期：2026年10月24日（星期六）
時間：下午3時至下午5時
地點：九龍尖沙咀香港文化中心行政大樓四樓會議室AC1
講座以英語講述，歡迎現場或網上參與。
(Zoom網上連結將於活動前以電郵通知已報名者)
網上報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13740305
如有查詢，請聯絡書院輔導處王先生（電話：3943-1690 電郵：
jackwong@cuhk.edu.hk
）或梁小姐（電話：3943-9589 電郵：
angelaleung@cuhk.edu.hk
）。
“New Asia Lectures on Confucianism” is generously sponsored by the Moonchu Foundation. The 12th New Asia Lectures on Confucianism will be held in October 2026, and it is our honor to have invited Professor Franklin Perkins to be our speaker. Professor Perkins is the Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. Details of the lectures are as follows:
1st Lecture
Topic: Mengzi on What People Really Want
Moderator: Prof. David Chai, Department of Philosophy, CUHK
Date: 21 October 2026 (Wednesday)
Time: 6:30pm – 8:00pm
Venue: Sir Run Run Shaw Hall, CUHK
(This lecture will be held at the College Bi-weekly Assembly)
2nd Lecture
Topic: The Common Foundation for Early Confucian Ethics
Moderator: Prof. Zhihua Yao, Department of Philosophy, CUHK
Date: 22 October 2026 (Thursday)
Time: 4:30pm – 6:15pm
Venue: Cho Yiu Conference Hall, G/F, University Administration Building, CUHK
(This lecture is jointly organized by New Asia College and Department of Philosophy, CUHK)
3rd Lecture
Topic: The Relevance of Life After Death in Early Confucianism
Moderator: Prof. Zemian Zheng, Department of Philosophy, CUHK
Date: 24 October 2026 (Saturday)
Time: 3:00pm – 5:00pm
Venue: Function Room AC1, 4/F, Administration Building, Hong Kong Cultural Centre, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon
All lectures will be conducted in English.
Participation in person or via Zoom online is also welcome.
(A Zoom link will be sent to registrants by email before the event)
Online Registration:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13740305
For enquiries, please contact Mr. Jack Wong, Dean of Students’ Office (Tel: 3943-1690; Email:
jackwong@cuhk.edu.hk
) or Miss Angela Leung, Dean of Students’ Office (Tel: 3943-9589; Email:
angelaleung@cuhk.edu.hk
).

Ready to put your data analytics skills into action? This is your chance to showcase your expertise and collaborate with peers across disciplines!
The CUHK Library, in collaboration with the Data Science and Policy Studies Programme, is pleased to invite applications for the Data Analytics Practice Opportunity 2026/27. This initiative provides CUHK students with valuable hands-on experience working with real-world datasets and digitised records, empowering them to craft compelling stories through data visualisation and analytics tools. Participants will also have the opportunity to showcase their projects and findings during Data Excellence Week 2027.
Application Deadline: 21 October 2026 (Wed)
Teams of 2-3 members
Eligibility: CUHK full-time undergraduate or postgraduate students
Allowance: HKD 8,000 per team

Take Charge of Your Health: Central Obesity Programme for Adults Aged 40–64 [HK$200 Coupon]   40–64歲健康新開始：參與中央肥胖改善計劃，完成可獲HK$200現金券！ - Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
From: MA Chun hin

邀請參加本項研究
初步證據顯示, 間歇性飲食（INTD）和高強度間歇運動（HIIE）在改善心血管代謝健康和減重方面存在協同作用。本研究旨在探討INTD和HIIE對體力活動不足的中央肥胖成人的心血管健康影響。
受試者招募
本研究的目標人群為香港體力活動不足的中年成年人（年齡40至64歲），並且具有中央肥胖。中央肥胖將定義為男性腰圍達90厘米（cm）或以上，女性腰圍達80厘米或以上。如果您對任何列出的條件有疑問，請諮詢研究人員。
問卷網址
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5q1f0ammiljEDOu
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
馬先生
WhatsApp: 39436085
Email: ericaaama@cuhk.edu.hk
Invitation to Participate in Research Study
Preliminary evidence has suggested a synergistic interaction effect of intermittent dieting (INTD) and high intensity interval exercise (HIIE) on cardio-metabolic health and weight loss. This study aims to examine the effects of INTD and HIIE and intermittent dieting for cardiometabolic and cardiovascular fitness in physically inactive adults with central obesity.
Participant Recruitment
The target population of the proposed study will be physically inactive middle-aged adults (aged 40–64 years) with central obesity in Hong Kong. Central obesity will be defined as having a waist circumference 90 centimeters (cm) or above for men and 80 cm or above for women. If you are unsure about any of the listed conditions, then you should consult with the researchers.
Survey address
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5q1f0ammiljEDOu

Announcements
HK$500 reward! Recruiting Cantonese speakers for a language learning study  招募廣東話母語者參與語言學習研究，成功完成測試可獲500hkd酬謝 - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: CHEN Xinwen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
xinwen.chen@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
實驗時間：
需來两次：一節爲腦電實驗，約3小時；一節爲行為實驗，約2.5小時。
實驗內容：
①腦電實驗：
佩戴腦電帽
（對人體安全無害）完成語言學習任務
腦電實驗中，您將會接受
經顱光生物調節（tPBM）
：此儀器用一束微弱的光刺激額頭，同樣對人體完全無害，不會有任何感覺，已獲得大學和醫院的使用批准，這種儀器已被證實可以有效提高記憶力。
②行為實驗：完成一系列語言和認知測試；
③填寫問卷。
實驗地點：
①腦電/光調節實驗在香港中文大學王福元樓406A進行；②行為實驗在香港中文大學梁銶琚樓G/F進行
兩次實驗結束後，會支付500港元被試費用。
參與者需要符合以下要求：
1. 年齡18-30歲，非心理學/語言學專業。
2. 母語為廣東話；
3. 聽力、視力或矯正視力正常；
4. 無腦損傷、癲癇等神經類疾病，無頭皮外傷或感染；
5. 右利手；
6. 實驗時間身體健康，無感冒發燒咳嗽等狀況；
7. 實驗前要保證充足的睡眠，精力充沛認真負責完成實驗；
8. 實驗前24小時未服用大量茶、咖啡等飲料；實驗前不要有劇烈的體育活動；
9. 實驗前兩週不能染髮；
10. 實驗當天需要洗頭，不能化妝，額頭不要塗防曬霜、隔離霜等。
如有任何問題，請聯繫：xinwen.chen@cuhk.edu.hk
報名連結：
http://137.189.158.12/limesurvey/index.php?r=survey/index&sid=813414&lang=zh-Hant-HK
Experiment Duration:
You will need to visit twice: one session for the EEG experiment (approximately 3 hours) and one session for the behavioral experiment (approximately 2.5 hours).
Experiment Details:
1. EEG experiment: Completing language learning tasks with an
EEG
cap
Participants in the EEG study will receive
transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM)
: This device uses a weak beam of light to stimulate the forehead. It is completely harmless to the human body and causes no sensation. This type of device has been proven to effectively improve memory and has been approved for use by universities and hospitals.
2. Behavioral experiment: Completing a series of language and cognitive tests;
3. Completion of questionnaires.
Experiment Locations: 406A, Wong Foo Yuan Building OR G/F, Leung Kau Kui Building, CUHK
After completing
both sessions
, participants will receive a reimbursement of
HK$500
.
Eligibility Requirements:
Aged 18–30; not majoring in psychology or linguistics.
Cantonese native speaker.
Normal hearing and vision, or corrected-to-normal vision.
No history of brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological conditions; no scalp injuries or infections.
Right-handed (i.e., habitually writes or uses chopsticks with the right hand).
In good health on the day of the experiment (no cold, fever, cough, etc.).
Well-rested before the experiment, and able to complete the task attentively and responsibly.
No consumption of large amounts of tea, coffee, or similar drinks within 24 hours prior; no intense physical activity before the experiment.
No hair dyeing within two weeks before the experiment.
Please wash your hair and do not wear makeup or apply sunscreen/primer/foundation on the forehead on the day of the experiment.
For inquiries, please contact: xinwen.chen@cuhk.edu.hk
Registration link:
http://137.189.158.12/limesurvey/index.php?r=survey/index&sid=813414&lang=zh-Hant-HK

MSc in Clinical Gerontology and End-of-Life Care
equips students with advanced knowledge and practical skills in gerontology, palliative care, and end-of-life care. It is designed for professionals in social welfare, healthcare, and related sectors who wish to strengthen their practice and expand their career opportunities.The programme is designed to support
healthcare professionals
and
social workers
.
The 2027/28 academic year will commence in September 2027. Students may choose to pursue the programme on
1-year full-time
or
2-year part-time
basis.
臨牀老人學與寧養關顧理學碩士
課程涵蓋老年學、認知障礙症照顧、紓緩治療及安寧照顧等範疇，旨在提升社福、醫護及相關專業人士的知識與實務能力，以回應人口老化帶來的服務需要。課程適合
醫療衛生專業人員及社工
。 2027/28學年將於2027年9月開始, 學生可選擇入讀1年全日制或2年兼讀制課程。

title: EEG Experiment: 1.5h for 120 HKD (Native Mandarin Speakers) 【普通话母语者招募中】你的大脑是怎么读中文的？来实验室告诉我们
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Announcements
EEG Experiment: 1.5h for 120 HKD (Native Mandarin Speakers) 【普通话母语者招募中】你的大脑是怎么读中文的？来实验室告诉我们 - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Yiting WANG
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你好！
我们诚挚地邀请你参加一项关于语言认知的脑电（EEG）实验。任务很简单：
来实验室看一些视频
。我们会记录你的脑电波，看看母语阅读时大脑有多忙碌！
本实验室使用临床级安全的脑电图系统，收集人自身产生的微弱生物电并绘制成波形图，不会对人体产生伤害。有任何安全顾虑都可以和研究人员联系了解：Miss WANG, yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk
实验时长
：约1.5小时
实验内容：
1）佩戴脑电设备，参加互动实验，观看一些视频并用键盘按键做出反应；2）填写一些问卷。
实验地点：
中文大学梁銶琚楼G层（语言学系）G34实验室。
实验结束后，会通过转数快支付
120港元
被试费用。
参与者需要符合以下要求
：
1.
18-30
岁
，来自中国大陆，母语为汉语普通话；
2. 视力（矫正后）正常，无干涩等眼部不适；
3. 听力正常；
4. 无脑损伤、癫痫等神经类疾病，无头皮外伤或感染；
5. 无身体残疾；
6. 近2个月内无染发，实验当天不化妆，实验当天在家自行洗头；
7. 可以接受在头发头皮上涂抹特制的导电膏体（实验室配备专门的洗头房，供您实验结束之后洗净吹干）；
8. 非心理学、语言学专业；
9. 右利手（写字、用筷子等习惯使用右手）；
10. 没有参加过此实验的相关实验（如果不确定可以联系主试确认：Miss WANG, yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk)
报名链接
：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9FZeVuIlwkN6tKK
香港中文大学语言学及现代语言系
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Hi there!
Ever wondered how does your brain read Chinese?
We’re recruiting
native Mandarin speakers
for an EEG experiment. The task is simple:
come to the lab and watch some videos
. We’ll record your brainwaves to see how busy your brain gets when processing your native language.
Duration of the experiment
: The experiment duration is approximately 1.5 hours
Experiment content:
1) wearing EEG devices, reading some Chinese sentences and responding with keyboard keys; 2) filling out some questionnaires.
Experiment location
: Room G34, G/F, K.K. Leung Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
The subject fee of
HK$120
will be paid via FPS (other approaches are supported) at the end of the experiment.
Participants need to meet the
following requirements
:
1. native Mandarin Chinese speaker, 18-30 years old;
2. have normal vision (after correction) and no eye discomfort such as dryness;
3. have normal hearing;
4. no brain injury, epilepsy or other neurological diseases, no scalp trauma or infection;
5. no physical disability;
6. no hair coloring in the last 2 months, no make-up on the day of the experiment, and washing hair at home by themselves on the day of the experiment;
7. can accept the application of special conductive paste on the hair scalp (the laboratory is equipped with a special hair washing room; participants can wash hair at the end of the experiment);
8. non-psychology / linguistics majors;
9. right-handed (writing, using chopsticks, etc.);
10. have not participated in the preparatory experiment for this experiment. If you are not sure, you can contact the experimenter to confirm: Miss WANG, yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk
Enrolment link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9FZeVuIlwkN6tKK
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages, The Chinese University of Hong Kong

Prof. CAI Zhenguang

本实验室使用临床级安全的脑电图系统，收集人自身产生的微弱生物电并绘制成波形图，不会对人体产生伤害。有任何安全顾虑都可以和研究人员联系了解：Miss WANG, yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk
实验时长
：约1.5小时
实验内容：
1）佩戴脑电设备，参加互动实验，观看一些视频并用键盘按键做出反应；2）填写一些问卷。
实验地点：
中文大学梁銶琚楼G层（语言学系）G34实验室。
实验结束后，会通过转数快支付
120港元
被试费用。
参与者需要符合以下要求
：
1.
18-30
岁
，来自中国大陆，母语为汉语普通话；
2. 视力（矫正后）正常，无干涩等眼部不适；
3. 听力正常；
4. 无脑损伤、癫痫等神经类疾病，无头皮外伤或感染；
5. 无身体残疾；
6. 近2个月内无染发，实验当天不化妆，实验当天在家自行洗头；
7. 可以接受在头发头皮上涂抹特制的导电膏体（实验室配备专门的洗头房，供您实验结束之后洗净吹干）；
8. 非心理学、语言学专业；
9. 右利手（写字、用筷子等习惯使用右手）；
10. 没有参加过此实验的相关实验（如果不确定可以联系主试确认：Miss WANG, yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk)

Hi there!

native Mandarin speakers
for an EEG experiment. The task is simple:
come to the lab and watch some videos
. We’ll record your brainwaves to see how busy your brain gets when processing your native language.

: The experiment duration is approximately 1.5 hours

ma
nagement

【Investigate Structural Variations (SVs) in Autism Spectrum (ASD) and Related Endophenotypes】
. It aims to investigate the association of mutations in genes, as well as other potential structural variants, with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in individuals from Hong Kong.

From: School of Journalism and Communication
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
com@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Communication Seminar Series - Community-Engaged AI in Civic and Social Organizations: Meaningful and Democratic Communication Co-Creation for Health Equity and Social Good
Date: 23 October 2026 (Friday)
Time: 10:30 am-12:00 nn
Venue: C-Centre (NAH313, Humanities Building, CUHK)
Speaker:
Prof. Andy Tan
Associate Professor
Annenberg School for Communication
University of Pennsylvania, USA
Bio:
Andy Tan is Associate Professor of Communication at the Annenberg School for Communication of the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Tan’s research program is aimed at advancing communication science to achieve health equity for all. His work examines the impact of marketing, media, and public health messages on health behaviors and outcomes among diverse populations including young adults, socioeconomically disadvantaged, and lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) populations. He conducts community-engaged research involving organizations that serve LGBT communities to design and develop culturally appropriate communication interventions that are informed by persuasion and message effects theories, social determinants of health frameworks, and implementation science. The goal of this work is to translate this knowledge into scalable and culturally sensitive communication interventions to alleviate tobacco- and cancer-related health disparities. Dr. Tan is the recipient of awards for his communication and health equity research including the 2025 Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers (PECASE), the American Public Health Association Health Equity Award in 2021, and was inducted as a Fellow by the Society for Research in Nicotine and Tobacco in 2026.
Abstract:
Civic and social organizations are embedded within local communities and provide essential health and social services to individuals, families, and communities. Staff of civic and social organizations have a deep understanding of the issues and community assets, are trusted messengers, and have shared lived experiences with the communities they serve. However, they often have limited resources for health communication and to create professional quality education and outreach campaigns. Over 2 summers (2025-2026), the Annenberg School partnered with COLOURS, a Philadelphia-based organization serving BIPOC and LGTBQ+ residents for 35 years, to design, test, and deploy
OurSpace
, an AI-supported workspace. In the summer of 2026, the study piloted
OurSpace
for COLOURS staff to plan for and promote an outreach event for medical and social needs case managers serving people living with HIV. In this talk, the speaker introduces the Community-Engaged AI lifecycle, describe the underlying rationale of
OurSpace
’s design, trace the evolution of its affordances, and deploying
OurSpace
in ways that ensure AI amplifies rather than substitutes local knowledge and experience of civic social organizations. Using examples of products created by COLOURS staff, observation notes, surveys, and qualitative inputs, the speaker discusses the strengths, limitations, and next steps for responsible and meaningful use of
OurSpace
to achieve health equity and social good in communication research and practice.

Communication Seminar Series - Community-Engaged AI in Civic and Social Organizations: Meaningful and Democratic Communication Co-Creation for Health Equity and Social Good
Date: 23 October 2026 (Friday)
Time: 10:30 am-12:00 nn
Venue: C-Centre (NAH313, Humanities Building, CUHK)
Speaker:
Prof. Andy Tan
Associate Professor
Annenberg School for Communication
University of Pennsylvania, USA
Bio:
Andy Tan is Associate Professor of Communication at the Annenberg School for Communication of the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Tan’s research program is aimed at advancing communication science to achieve health equity for all. His work examines the impact of marketing, media, and public health messages on health behaviors and outcomes among diverse populations including young adults, socioeconomically disadvantaged, and lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) populations. He conducts community-engaged research involving organizations that serve LGBT communities to design and develop culturally appropriate communication interventions that are informed by persuasion and message effects theories, social determinants of health frameworks, and implementation science. The goal of this work is to translate this knowledge into scalable and culturally sensitive communication interventions to alleviate tobacco- and cancer-related health disparities. Dr. Tan is the recipient of awards for his communication and health equity research including the 2025 Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers (PECASE), the American Public Health Association Health Equity Award in 2021, and was inducted as a Fellow by the Society for Research in Nicotine and Tobacco in 2026.
Abstract:
Civic and social organizations are embedded within local communities and provide essential health and social services to individuals, families, and communities. Staff of civic and social organizations have a deep understanding of the issues and community assets, are trusted messengers, and have shared lived experiences with the communities they serve. However, they often have limited resources for health communication and to create professional quality education and outreach campaigns. Over 2 summers (2025-2026), the Annenberg School partnered with COLOURS, a Philadelphia-based organization serving BIPOC and LGTBQ+ residents for 35 years, to design, test, and deploy
OurSpace
, an AI-supported workspace. In the summer of 2026, the study piloted
OurSpace
for COLOURS staff to plan for and promote an outreach event for medical and social needs case managers serving people living with HIV. In this talk, the speaker introduces the Community-Engaged AI lifecycle, describe the underlying rationale of
OurSpace
’s design, trace the evolution of its affordances, and deploying
OurSpace
in ways that ensure AI amplifies rather than substitutes local knowledge and experience of civic social organizations. Using examples of products created by COLOURS staff, observation notes, surveys, and qualitative inputs, the speaker discusses the strengths, limitations, and next steps for responsible and meaningful use of
OurSpace
to achieve health equity and social good in communication research and practice.

Announcements
.【 $250 Coupon 】Recruiting Children (aged 11 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and Children's Emotional Health Development Study 誠意邀請11歲或以下兒童參加腸道微生物及兒童心智發展的研究-Department of Psychiatry  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
oscarwhwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

研究題目
：比較不同有氧運動訓練對超重或肥胖絕經後女性代謝及循環血液指標影響的隨機對照試驗
親愛的女士：
您好！
隨着年齡增長與絕經後的荷爾蒙變化，您是否覺得體重逐漸增加、脂肪容易囤積，或者開始擔心體脂、血脂等健康指標？香港中文大學體育運動科學系目前正開展一項研究以了解不同有氧運動訓練對絕經後超重或肥胖女性代謝健康的影響。我們誠邀符合條件的華人女性參與，一起通過科學運動重拾健康！
參與本研究，您將免費獲得：
1. 全面身體成分評估：精準檢測體脂率、肌肉量、內臟脂肪等。

華人女性，且已自然絕經 12 個月或以上（距離最後一次月經少於 6 年）。
體型偏胖（BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² 或 體脂率 > 30%，以實驗室測試為準）。

過去 3 個月體重相對穩定，且無嚴重運動禁忌（如嚴重心臟病、中風等）。

The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong,
Sports Nutrition and Physical Activity Laboratory,
sincerely invites you to participate in an exercise intervention study! This study will help us understand your exercise metabolic performance and improve your metabolic health.
Study Title
: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing the Effects of Different Aerobic Exercise Training on Metabolic and Circulating Blood Indicators in Postmenopausal Women with overweight or obesity
Dear Madam:
With aging and postmenopausal hormonal changes, do you feel that your weight is gradually increasing, fat is easily accumulated, or you begin to worry about health indicators such as body fat and blood lipids? The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a study to understand the effects of different aerobic exercise training on metabolic health in postmenopausal women with overweight or obesity. We sincerely invite eligible Chinese women to participate and regain health together through scientific exercise!
By participating in this study, you will receive for free:
1. Comprehensive body composition assessment: accurate measurement of body fat percentage, muscle mass, visceral fat, etc.
2. Professional blood indicator testing: understand your core metabolic indicators such as blood lipids and blood glucose.
3. Expert-level exercise capacity test: accurately measure your exercise metabolic performance to evaluate your physical fitness and metabolic response.
4. 12 weeks of free exercise guidance: full follow‑up by professional researchers to ensure exercise safety and effectiveness.
We are looking for:
1. Chinese women who have been naturally postmenopausal for 12 months or more (less than 6 years since the last menstrual period).
2. Are overweight or obese (BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² or body fat percentage > 30%; will be confirmed by laboratory testing).
3. Are usually physically inactive (less than 150 minutes of moderate‑intensity physical activity, less than 75 minutes of vigorous‑intensity physical activity per week, or an equivalent combination).
4. Have had relatively stable body weight in the past 3 months, and have no serious contraindications to exercise (e.g., severe heart disease, stroke, etc.).
⏳ What do you need to do? (3 assessments + 12‑week intervention training)
This study lasts 12 weeks. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to a
control group
,
aerobic
exercise group A,
or
aerobic exercise group B
. During the period, you will need to visit the laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong for 3 assessments, including: questionnaire surveys, fasting venous blood draw, finger‑prick blood sampling, body composition measurement, and exercise metabolic testing. To reduce discomfort during testing, the exercise metabolic test will be conducted separately from other health tests. Throughout the study, you will need to come to the laboratory
6 times.
12‑week intervention training: 3 times per week, 40‑70 minutes per session, for 12 weeks.
Upon completion of the study, you will receive a HK$150 shopping voucher and a health report.
Trial location: G02 Office, Ground Floor, Kwok Sports Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong

If you have any questions, please contact the research team:
Study coordinator: Ms. He (WhatsApp: +852 5984 8824)
Supervising professor: Prof. Stephen Heung-sang WONG (Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Wishing you good health!

title: [Max. HKD$1200] Recruiting Native Cantonese-speaking Grandparents with hearing loss and Grandchildren for an Interaction Experiment [最高可獲HKD$1200][長者認知及聽力測試報告; + 兒童IQ智商測試報告] 招募聽力損失長者及其孫子女參與互動實驗
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Announcements
[Max. HKD$1200] Recruiting Native Cantonese-speaking Grandparents with hearing loss and Grandchildren for an Interaction Experiment [最高可獲HKD$1200][長者認知及聽力測試報告; + 兒童IQ智商測試報告] 招募聽力損失長者及其孫子女參與互動實驗 - Brain and Mind Institute
From: LEUNG Mei Yee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
我們是
香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（BMI）
的研究團隊。我們團隊誠摯邀請有聽力損失的長者及其孫子女來參與一項互動研究。
參與者需符合以下條件：
長者：
65歲或以上，存在聽力損失，
無其他已知認知障礙症狀， 且
有意願配戴助聽器
孩童：
6-9歲
，無其他已知發展問題，母語為廣東話
實驗內容：本實驗共分為兩節（每節約1.5至2小時）：
- 第一節：長者將獨自參與一項
認知及聽力檢測
（當日孫子女無需到場）
- 第二節：長者將與孫子女一同進行
簡單遊戲
，期間我們將使用安全且非侵入性的
「近紅外光譜儀」（fNIRS）
進行腦部掃描
- 請注意：參與者必須先完成第一節的實驗，且結果符合研究要求，方會獲邀參與第二節的實驗
完成整個實驗後，您可獲得：
- 長者：一份
認知能力測試報告
+ 一份
純音聽力測試報告
- 孩童：一份
非語言智商測試報告
+ 一份
價值HKD$80的禮物
報酬：
現金HKD$400-1200
，以及免費停車券（如適用）
實驗地點：香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（位於校園內）
如您對本研究感興趣，請點擊以下連結填寫報名表格：
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
如祖孫兩位初步符合條件，我們將會儘快與您聯絡！
如有疑問，請發送電郵至 meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk，
亦可致電或Whatsapp 95867123 查詢。
我們期待你的參與！
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We are researchers from the
Brain and Mind Institute (BMI) at the Chinese University of Hong Kong
. Our team sincerely invites grandparents with hearing loss and their grandchildren for a social interaction study.
Participants need to be:
- Grandparent:
65+ years old with hearing loss
, with no other diagnosed cognitive impairment, interested in fitting hearing aids
- Grandchild:
6-9 years old
with no other developmental problems; speaking Cantonese as the first language
What is involved? The experiment consists of two sessions (approx. 1.5-2 hours each):
- Session 1: The grandparent will participate alone in a
cognitive and hearing test
. (The grandchild does not need to attend)
- Session 2: The grandparent and grandchild will participate together in some
simple games
while using
fNIRS
(
functional near-infrared spectroscopy
, safe and non-invasive!!!) brain scanning device
- NOTE: Participants must first complete Session 1 and meet the study's requirements to be invited to Session 2
What you'll get (upon completion of the entire study):
- For the grandparent:
A cognitive test report
and
a pure-tone audiometry
(hearing test) report
- For the child:
An non-verbal IQ test report
and
a gift (~HKD$80)
Reward:
HKD$400-1200 allowance
and free parking ticket.
Location: Brain and Mind Institute, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (In campus).
If you are interested in our study, please fill in the form below via the following link:
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
We will contact you afterwards if the dyad are suitable.
For inquiries, please contact: meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk,
call or Whatsapp 95867123.
We look forward to your participation!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Mooncake Boxes Recycling Program 2026  - Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office
From: Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
中秋節將至，我們歡度佳節的同時，各種的送禮及慶祝活動往往會產生大量垃圾。為減少節日期間的垃圾，中大今年繼續參與綠領行動「月餅盒回收大行動」，收集到的月餅盒將送往環保署核准的回收商進行本地循環再造。
***中大收集日期：2026年9月28日（一 ）至10月9日（五）***
***月餅盒回收箱位置：康本國際學術園地下大堂***
回收指引：紙製及金屬製的月餅盒均可回收（請移除所有包裝物料並妥善處理）
如有查詢，請聯絡社會責任及可持續發展處（3943 3972/
srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
）。
As the Mid-Autumn Festival approaches, we will enjoy the delicious mooncakes and collect some mooncake boxes.  Instead of discarding these boxes, we can recycle them and give them a new purpose.  This year, CUHK continues to participate in the Greeners Action’s Mooncake Boxes Recycling Program.  The collected boxes will be processed by the EPD-approved recyclers for local recycling initiatives.
***CUHK Collection Period: 28 September (Monday) – 9 October 2026 (Friday) ***
***Collection Box Location:
G/F lobby, Yasumoto International Academic Park
***
Recycling guidelines: paper and metal boxes are acceptable (please remove any packaging materials and recycle them appropriately)
For enquiries, please contact the Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office (3943 3972/
srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

title: ( Receive up to HK$400Allowance!) Recruiting young adults (aged 18–24)for online sleep and mental health intervention with individualized support 誠邀18至24歲青年參加網上睡眠及心理健康課程，仲有個人化的指導（最高可獲得$400津貼！）
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/09
»
Announcements
( Receive up to HK$400Allowance!) Recruiting young adults (aged 18–24)for online sleep and mental health intervention with individualized support 誠邀18至24歲青年參加網上睡眠及心理健康課程，仲有個人化的指導（最高可獲得$400津貼！） - Department of Psychiatry
From: Winifred Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式的認知行為治療結合晝夜節律改善大學生的睡眠及情緒。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲在學青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 18歲至24歲大專生
2. 有失眠症狀及遲睡傾向(凌晨12點後才睡覺)
3.  過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
∎ 填寫網上評估問卷
∎佩戴睡眠手錶及填寫睡眠日記
∎完成 7 日簡短錄音錄影紀錄當下狀態（每日兩次，每次約１—２分鐘）
∎手機應用程式上的網上治療課程​ ，共6個單元，​每一星期睇一個單元 （15-30分鐘）
∎在完成治療​後的一星期及６個月後，會邀請你再填寫網上評估問卷及和配戴睡眠手錶
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 吳小姐) 查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile app-based cognitive behavioral therapy program combined with a circadian rhythm intervention in improving sleep and mental health among college/university students. We would like to invite participants aged between 18 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1.  College or university students aged between 18-24 years
2. Reporting symptoms of insomnia and a delayed sleep pattern, typically falling asleep after midnight.
3. Do not receive psychological, behavioural, or pharmacological treatment for insomnia or emotional problems in the past three months.
What will you do?
∎ Complete online questionnaires
∎ Wear the actigraphy watch and keep a sleep diary
∎ Record brief audio and video entries about your current state for 7 consecutive days (twice daily, 1–2 minutes each)
∎ Complete a  6-week intervention program through a mobile app-based  (one module per week,   15–30 minutes per module).
∎ Complete follow-up assessments and wear the actigraphy watch one week and six months after the intervention.
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 Miss Ng).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/
